articles.title: Report finds workers are staying around at their jobs — but many say that's because they feel stuck
articles.content: Workday study finds workers feel "stuck" in their roles due to lack of prospects European markets have higher two-year retention job rate than the global average But many workers say they feel less supported by their employers Despite widespread promises that AI is going to make workers happier and more productive, new research has found many are feeling less confident in their future. Workday's European Workforce Report found that across the continent, retention rates are rising, and in fact are higher than the global average - but AI may be having a more negative effect than leaders might think. Although retention rates seem encouraging, the report found workers feel less supported by their employer, with many saying they feel underappreciated and even stuck in their current role with no chance of moving forward. Work work work Workday's report found every European market it analyzed has a higher two-year retention rate than the global average of 69.6%, with Germany leading the way at 78.8%. Yet more than a third (34%) of workers in key markets including the UK, France, and Germany say they feel stuck in their current role due to a lack of prospects in a weak job market. Many of these workers also said they feel less supported by their employers, with just over half (54%) saying they feel their employer cares about them as a person, compared with 59% globally. Despite three-quarters (75%) of workers saying they know which skills they need to succeed, a much lower number (62%) say their employer is actually helping them build the skills they will need next. And despite most workers admitting they have received AI training from their employer, fewer than four in 10 in the UK (37%), France (36%), and Germany (39%) expect AI to create new opportunities in their careers. Ironically, the study also found many job seekers are now using AI tools to look for a new role - with 84% admitting so - but only 34% said AI led them to apply for more jobs. “Europe’s companies are holding on to their people, and on paper that looks like a strength,” said Angelique De Vries-Schipperijn, president, EMEA, Workday. “But when a third of workers say they’re staying because they feel stuck, leaders should hear that as a warning. AI is hanging many jobs, and the people who stay need to see where they fit in what comes next.”
articles.author: Mike Moore

articles.title: Most people skip this exercise, but it's essential for strong abs and hips over 60 — and it's not crunches, sit-ups, or planks
articles.content: As you get older, a strong core becomes even more important to help you maintain balance and stability and avoid injury. But the types of core exercises you enjoyed at 20 might not be the types you enjoy today, and for me personally, at 35, I now prefer low-impact, deep core exercises over typical moves like sit-ups, crunches, or planks. For that reason, I wanted to share one exercise I love for strengthening your core and hips while remaining low-impact for your spine. One of the best core exercises I use with my dad, who is nearing 73, looks simple but really blasts your core and deep stabilizer muscles. It also strengthens your hip flexors, which are important muscles for walking and running. Read on to learn more. What is the exercise? As a reminder, this exercise is beginner-friendly. Still, if you're pregnant, postpartum, or dealing with an injury, it’s always best to seek personalized advice from an expert who knows you and your body. I like exercises that keep your spine straight and stable while teaching the various muscles that form your core to maintain and control tension. So, rather than peddling out endless sit-ups, which flex your spine over and over, I recommend trying leg openers. If you're unsure what "bracing" your core means, I teach you how with a 5-minute bracing routine . Here’s how to perform leg openers with proper form: A post shared by Tom's Guide Fitness | Workout Tips & Gear (@tomsguidefitness) A photo posted by Sit with your legs extended in front of you and your spine tall and straight, keeping your gaze ahead. For extra support, rest against a wall Place your hands gently on the ground, behind your head, on your hips, or crossed over your chest Brace your stomach, then lift one leg to hover above the ground, pause, then slowly open your leg to the side, working the outer glute, hips and inner thigh Pause at your end range of motion, then slowly return to center and lower your leg Complete 6-8 reps on one side, then switch. If this feels too intense, alternate sides. Aim for 2-3 sets. Avoid hunching or dumping into your torso. Imagine a piece of string running along your spine and coming out of the crown of your head. Now imagine someone pulling that string to lift you. Move slowly and with control, using your braced stomach to maintain your upright position. You can slightly lean back, but try not to do so excessively. Are leg openers good for the back? (Image credit: Getty Images) Yes, which is why I use it with older clients regularly. The move teaches proper posture and spinal alignment as you keep your shoulders stacked over your hips and avoid hunching or rounding. This also requires your core muscles to activate to hold you upright and keep you stable; a strong, active core protects your lower back. Leg openers also work your hip flexors, which are important muscles for lifting your knees, allowing you to walk and run. As you abduct the hip, your outer glutes and adductors also switch on; your glutes help stabilize the pelvis, and the adductors run along your inner thighs, sometimes referred to as the groin. This exercise is much friendlier for your lower back than moves like sit-ups, as you can support your lower back if needed, and you don't need to use any extreme range of motion, like hyperextension or flexion, or spinal compression. This move also teaches you to control the movement you generate, increasing time under tension , or how long your muscles work, to build endurance. I like to count four seconds out with a one-second pause and a four-second count back in. If you notice you're leaning back too much, position yourself against a wall to prevent this, as you want to maintain a strong L-shaped position with your body. A soft bend in the working leg is fine if you have tight hamstrings. Follow Tom's Guide fitness on Instagram for more workouts, routines, tips, and tricks. articles.title: Uncensored AI models are thriving on code hosting platforms
articles.content: Uncensored large language models (ULLMs) capable of producing harmful content are readily available at popular model-hosting websites, calling into question AI industry commitments to safety. Researchers affiliated with University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in the US and Nanyang Technological University in Singapore have analysed 22,096 ULLMs collected from five major LLM hosting platforms. As described in their paper , "Characterizing the Ecosystem of Open-Source Uncensored Large Language Models: Supply Chain, Governance, and Risks," authors Zilong Lin, Zichuan Li, Xiaojing Liao, and XiaoFeng Wang found that uncensored LLMs are easy to obtain from hosting platforms like US-based Hugging Face, Kaggle, and John Snow Labs, and China-based OpenCSG and ModelScope. What's more, these unrestrained models have been deployed through applications, GitHub projects, and model routing platforms like Open Router, and users of those apps or services may not be aware of the nature of the underlying LLM. "Uncensored LLMs generally refer to LLMs whose content filtering or refusal safeguards are absent, removed, or weakened, allowing them to respond to requests that aligned models may refuse," the paper explains. Zilong Lin, lead author and assistant professor of computer science at the University of Missouri-Kansas City, told The Register that open source LLM hosting platforms like Hugging Face play a similar role to code hosting services like GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg in the open source community by enabling sharing, modification, and redistribution of code artifacts. "However, unlike traditional software, whose behavior can often be examined through source code analysis, the safety alignment of LLMs is difficult to assess directly from their model files," Lin explained. "Evaluating whether an LLM has adequate safety safeguards typically requires deploying the model and testing its responses to potentially harmful prompts, which involves substantial computational and financial costs." Lin said this makes the identification and assessment of LLM safety particularly challenging, particularly given the large number of models available. That's why he and his colleagues chose to study the space through publicly available model metadata. Even popular commercial LLMs that are purportedly "aligned" – to some standard not everyone accepts – may respond to prompts with content deemed harmful. The US Government Accountability Office just released a report that found Claude, Grok, ChatGPT, and Gemini can be coaxed to provide information that would help with the planning of a terror attack. To highlight the consequences of AI advice, the GAO points to news reports indicating that generative AI helped enable the creation of an explosive device in a January 2025 attack on a Las Vegas hotel and the planning of a February 2026 mass shooting in British Columbia, Canada. The issue with open weight LLMs is that anyone with modest technical skills (or just cluelessly assisted by a compliant LLM) can apply techniques like toxic training/fine-tuning (TTFT) or de-aligned training/fine-tuning (DTFT) to datasets that haven't been safe, in order to produce models with reduced or removed refusal behavior. Examples include toxicqa-Llama2-13B and WizardLM-7B-Uncensored . A more recent technique called refusal-direction ablation (or abliteration, e.g., Daredevil-8B-abliterated ) dilutes refusal training to make the model less likely to refuse requests. Uncensored (or simply less restrictive) models have legitimate uses, sometimes ironically because commercial models are insufficiently permissive and refuse legitimate security analysis. Hugging Face, for example, had to resort to using Z.ai's less rule-encumbered GLM-5.2 to analyze the hacking of its infrastructure by OpenAI's irresponsibly unsupervised AI agents. But ULLMs can just as easily be misused to provide guidance about illegal activity, assist with malware development, or emit content that's harmful,…

articles.title: GTA 6 dev says Rockstar designed the wanted system so players ‘feel the seriousness of your actions,’ complete with ‘competent pursuit behaviours’ — ‘At times, we use unfit cop types that are easy to get away from, who might give up when chasing you’
articles.content: Grand Theft Auto 6 vice president of technology David Hynd says the wanted system was designed to make players "feel the seriousness of your actions" He explains that the system went through lots of iterations during development, as Rockstar thought the cops were "too easy or too hard" Hynd says "competent pursuit behaviours" were "crucial" to building the most authentic wanted system Grand Theft Auto 6 will feature a vastly improved, reactive wanted system compared to GTA 5 , which was designed to make players "feel the seriousness of your actions." Responding to questions sent directly to Rockstar by TechRadar Gaming, vice president of technology David Hynd said the law enforcement and crime system saw "lots and lots of iteration," as "there were many times throughout development where the cops were too easy or too hard." "We had to figure out which levers to pull to balance things out. And so we added a crazy amount of levers for the team to play with!" Hynd said. At lower star levels, Rockstar wanted the cops to feel "slightly different, but definitely easier," he explained, giving the team room to make the cops more realistic in terms of behaviour. "At times, we use unfit cop types that are easy to get away from, who might give up when chasing you," Hynd added. That's when Rockstar introduced the game's arrest/surrender systems at lower star levels; however, the team still wanted players to feel the heat if their actions get riskier. "On the opposite side of the fence, we wanted you to feel the seriousness of your actions at higher wanted levels as you need to commit some serious crimes to get your star level that high," Hynd said. The developer continued, saying some of the things that were "crucial to achieving this" included "competent pursuit behaviours." This meant that "cops had to be able to keep up in busy streets and drive similarly to the player," such as against traffic or off- road. "Once we had a suite of behaviours, we were happy with (ramming, PIT manoeuvres, boxing in, blocking in front, shooting out tyres, etc.), we were able to adapt and choose the best ones to orchestrate the kind of experience we wanted players to have," Hynd said. "We can decide how many units to dispatch, where to place roadblocks, and how aggressive cops should be at stopping you." GTA 6 finally launches tomorrow for PS5, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S, and if you've pre-ordered, you still have enough time to pre-load . If you haven't got around to it yet, here's your guide to the best places to buy GTA 6 .

articles.title: GameNative just fixed PC gaming on Pixels and Exynos-powered Galaxy phones
articles.content: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR The GameNative v1.4.1 release preview is now available and brings much better support for non-Snapdragon devices. The update specifically fixes major graphical problems on devices like the Pixel 6 to Pixel 10, as well as Exynos-powered Galaxy phones. This GameNative release also brings an Optimize feature that tunes your game based on preset goals. GameNative is still one of the best ways to locally run PC games on your Android device. The app works best on Snapdragon-powered devices, although the team previously introduced support for other chipmakers a while back. Now, the latest update brings great news if you’ve got a Pixel or Exynos-powered device. GameNative v1.4.1 has been released on GitHub as a preview, and it brings updated support for devices with Mali, PowerVR, and Xclipse graphics. The team specifically updated the “wrapper-gamenative” graphics driver. Check out the table below for a better idea of what’s been fixed.

articles.title: The Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited's TMR sticks, Hall Effect triggers and Command screen make it the pro PS5 controller I’ve been waiting for
articles.content: The Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited is one of the best PS5 controllers today, period. That’s the review. My job here is done. I jest, I jest! The R5U is simply phenomenal, whether you’re a casual or competitive esports gamer. Supremely precise TMR thumbsticks, dual-mode Hall Effect triggers, and plenty of customizable buttons, packed into an ergonomic body make the R5U extremely easy to recommend. In addition to that, the R5U comes fitted with a built-in screen for on-the-fly customization as well as a dock for simultaneously charging and displaying the controller. It naturally lacks DualSense features, like haptic feedback, and battery life is limited to just 10 hours. Are either of those dealbreakers? Not in the slightest. The R5U is a great step-up for those who own just the first-party DualSense. It’s a pro gamepad through and through. For the complete breakdown, read my full Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited review. Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited review: Cheat sheet What is it? A highly customizable PS5 controller with Hall Effect triggers and TMR thumbsticks Who is it for? Competitive gamers or even casuals who want a powerful third-party controller How much does it cost? $229 / £179 What do we like? The ergonomic design, phenomenal gaming performance, extensive hardware and software customization, and built-in screen What don’t we like? The battery life and omission of DualSense features Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited review: Specs Price $229 / £179 Layout PlayStation Shapes Connectivity 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth, USB-C wired Compatibility PlayStation 5, PC Triggers Hall Effect Thumbsticks TMR Back buttons Yes, four Polling rate 250Hz (PS5), 2,000Hz (PC) Dimensions 6.3 x 4.13 x 2.36 inches Weight 10.5oz Colors Black Battery (rated) 10 hours Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited review: The ups From its superb TMR thumbsticks and Hall Effect triggers to its degree of software and hardware customization, the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited is a formidable controller for PS5 players. Supremely precise TMR thumbsticks (Image credit: Tom's Guide) It wouldn’t be a pro-grade controller if it utilized traditional analog thumbsticks. The Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited is fitted with TMR (or Tunnel Magneto Resistance) thumbsticks, which achieve greater precision than their Hall Effect counterparts by using weak electromagnetic waves. TMR sensors can detect even the most minute movements — perfect for competitive gaming. The R5U is one of a handful of PS5 controllers to feature TMR sticks, like the Razer Raiju V3 Pro ($219), but I want every gamepad to have it. Of course, the R5U won’t make you better at esports overnight , but the TMR sticks’ precision is truly unmatched. I tested the controller by playing 007 First Light , Need for Speed Heat, and Ghost of Yotei on my PS5 Slim , and I was thoroughly impressed with the R5U. (Image credit: Tom's Guide) Proving responsive and accurate across all three titles, I appreciated being able to fine-tune my movements exactly the way I wanted. In 007 First Light, I was able to execute precise headshots while taking cover — multiple ones in succession, too, as the R5U’s sticks start and stop without any hiccups. Similarly, in Need for Speed Heat, I was able to make subtle steering corrections when racing at 200+ mph without overcorrecting or spinning out. TMR sticks (as well as Hall Effect ones) are also more durable than traditional analog thumbsticks, and they’re resistant to stick drift. As someone who has lost many controllers to it, that alone makes the R5U a worthy investment. Dual-mode Hall Effect triggers (Image credit: Tom's Guide) Alongside TMR thumbsticks, the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited features dual-mode Hall Effect triggers. Using the buttons on the R5U’s back, you can swap between two trigger modes: full-range long presses for millimeter-precise travel, and short microswitch clicks for mouse-like controls. articles.title: Google continues model chemistry experiment with Neon
articles.content: Google periodically tables new AI models named after elements, and its latest offering has the noble name "Neon." "Engineered for long-running agent workflows, Neon sustains performance through complex, tool-heavy tasks end-to-end — whether running standalone or acting as a fast, high-judgment Orchestrator directing parallel Hydrogen subagents in Google Antigravity," explained Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP at Google DeepMind and chief AI architect at Google, in a blog post . Neon emerged after Google last week emitted Hydrogen , after delivering Carbon two weeks earlier and wafting Argon out the door in late September. Unlike OpenAI's celestial more intuitive model naming scheme – Astra, Sol, Luna, and Terra – which maps celestial position to capability, Google's chemical soup doesn't suggest a specific hierarchy. To judge by price , Carbon or Argon would be Google's top tier model, based on non-discounted price that takes effect next month, each priced at $4/M input tokens, $20/M output. The Chocolate Factory refers to Carbon as "Our most capable reasoning model" while Argon is "Our efficient Gemini 4 frontier reasoning model … with faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Gemini 4 Carbon across complex coding, agentic, math, and science tasks." Yet Neon, the latest element in the mix, surpasses both in Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index , scoring 61 compared to Carbon at 60, Hydrogen at 54, and Argon at 50. At the same time, Neon costs less, at $3/M input tokens and $15/M output. That favorable pricing is all the more surprising in light of Google's willingness, as of two days ago , to let users of its Gemini services opt out of generative AI model training without losing their chat histories. Kavukcuoglu evidently recognizes the need to clarify its model rankings, an issue addressed in a blog post section titled "Where Neon sits in the Gemini 4 family." "While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency," he explains. "Neon delivers frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently." That may not really clarify which model is appropriate for which task and frankly Google is fine with that. As noted, Google Antigravity comes with an Orchestrator that decides how to spend your money for you by swapping models on the fly. As the company describes it, a developer might start a task using Carbon, which would write a plan, and hand the task off to Hydrogen to benefit from its token thrift. Antigravity does support model pinning , for those who know what they want. But Google, like other companies exploring model routing and orchestration, is fine with developers delegating decisions that affect billing to their trustworthy service provider. ®

articles.title: Verizon Black Friday deals discount my favorite phones — free iPhone 18 Pro, $480 off Galaxy S26 Ultra,and more
articles.content: Black Friday might be a week away, but that’s not stopping wireless carriers and retailers from giving some of my favorite phones very deep discounts ahead of the biggest shopping day of the year. That means flagship models like the iPhone 18 Pro, Galaxy S26 Ultra, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and more have various promotions attached to them — whether they’re free or come with discounted payment plans. These promotions make it much easier to pull the trigger on them, especially when prices in general are astronomical. Here are some of my favorite Verizon Black Friday deals available right now. articles.titleFa: محققان باگ‌های اجرای کد از راه دور در دیتابیس‌های PostgreSQL، MySQL و Oracle را نشان دادند
articles.summaryFa: یک محقق نشان داد که حساب‌های کاربری با سطح دسترسی کم در دیتابیس‌ها حتی بدون دسترسی به جدول‌های کاربردی نیز می‌توانند برای اجرای کد در سرور دیتابیس استفاده شوند. این آسیب‌پذیری‌ها شامل باگ‌های مربوط به خراب‌کردن حافظه در کد موتور SQL برای PostgreSQL، MySQL و ClickHouse بوده و یک زنجیره جداگانه برای Oracle که به دسترسی خاصی نیاز ندارد، نیز ارائه شده است.
articles.summaryEn: A researcher has demonstrated that low-privilege database accounts, which cannot read any application tables, can still be used to execute code on the database server. The exploits include memory-corruption bugs in the SQL engine code for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and ClickHouse, along with a separate Oracle chain that requires no specific access.

articles.title: Claude is cracking down on abusive users — and 1 in 3 Americans could be in for a surprise
articles.content: If you've ever lost your patience with Claude and let a few choice words fly, Anthropic has a new rule you should know about. The company behind the popular AI chatbot is cracking down on users who repeatedly abuse its models, and persistent offenders could find their conversations cut short. Anthropic's updated usage policy , which took effect November 12, prohibits sustained and needless abusive behavior toward Claude. The company says the rule targets extreme cases rather than everyday frustration or criticism, but it also gives Anthropic grounds to take action against users who cross the line. The change comes as new research reveals just how often Americans lose their patience with AI. According to an analysis of more than 8 million chatbot messages , one in three American AI chatbot users has sworn at or insulted ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude. And if you're hoping a few angry words will finally get an AI chatbot to follow your instructions, the research suggests you might be better off taking a different approach. What happens if you're abusive to Claude? (Image credit: Shutterstock) Anthropic's new policy explicitly prohibits "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior" toward its AI models. That doesn't mean Claude will shut down your conversation the moment you swear. Anthropic says the restriction applies to repeated cruelty without a clear purpose, not ordinary frustration, disagreements, creative writing or legitimate AI testing. The company has already given Claude the ability to end conversations with persistently abusive users on Claude.ai and Claude Code. Anthropic first introduced this capability in August 2025 as part of its research into AI welfare and says ending conversations will remain its primary response to this type of behavior. If Claude does end a conversation because of user behavior, users won't get locked out immediately. In most cases, they can start a new chat, provide feedback or edit and retry previous messages. Anthropic's broader usage policy also allows the company to issue warnings, limit or throttle access, suspend accounts or terminate access when it suspects policy violations. However, it has not said that occasional profanity will result in an account ban. Obviously, chatbots aren't human, and whether AI systems can have experiences that deserve moral consideration remains an open debate. Anthropic acknowledges that uncertainty but is choosing to establish limits on how people treat its models. One in three Americans has sworn at an AI chatbot (Image credit: Shutterstock) The timing of Anthropic's policy change is particularly interesting given how frequently people apparently get angry with AI. AI visibility platform Searchable analyzed more than 8 million messages sent to ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude by an opt-in panel of American users between September 2025 and September 2026. Its report found that 33% of users had sent at least one swear word, insult or slur to an AI chatbot during that period. The biggest trigger wasn't particularly surprising. Chatbots failing to follow instructions accounted for 19% of derogatory messages, followed by incorrect answers at 18% and misunderstood requests at 15%. Other frustrations included chatbots refusing requests, responding too slowly , producing unnecessarily long answers or repeating themselves. The research also uncovered some geographic differences. Nevada was the state where users directed the most derogatory language toward chatbots, while New Jersey was the politest. Among major metropolitan areas, Las Vegas ranked highest for swearing and insults, while New York ranked lowest. Men used roughly a third more derogatory language toward chatbots than women, while adults aged 35 to 44 were the most likely age group to use it, based on the rate of offensive words in their messages. Swearing at AI might not help you get a better answer (Image credit: Shutterstock) Arguably, the most useful finding has nothing to do with Anthropic's rules.…
articles.author: Amanda Caswell
articles.fingerprint: abusive americans claude could cracking down surprise users

articles.title: I’m clearing my countertops for holiday hosting, but these three appliances are staying
articles.content: If you’re hosting over the holiday season and you have a small kitchen, you’re probably racking your brain for more space. Even if you have a decent-sized layout, your countertops can quickly get cluttered with appliances, leaving no room to prep. That’s why I’m doing a pre-holiday purge and clearing my countertops to give me enough elbow room to work — and these are the only three hard-working appliances that earned their spot. Get ahead of the game (Image credit: Future) Every appliance you have staked out on your kitchen countertop takes up precious prep space — and during the holidays, you need every square inch of it. When you’re cooking a feast for a crowd, the last thing you want is the hassle of constantly shuffling gadgets around. Planning ahead and clearing your countertops before the festive season gets into full swing will ensure the only steam in your kitchen comes from the stove — not from you! The three appliance rule (Image credit: Shutterstock) While I am a secret neat freak and would love to have clear countertops, it simply isn’t practical, especially if you enjoy cooking and don’t rely on takeout. But I’ve found from experience, and from cooking a whole stack of festive dinners, that less is really more. That’s why I now keep my countertops reasonably tidy and rely on three main appliances instead of juggling a dozen gadgets. 1. Stand mixer (Image credit: KitchenAid) A stand mixer is always my number one kitchen appliance that stays out on my countertop. And while any stand mixer can help you whip, beat and knead, some have extra powers. If you opt for a stand mixer, like the KitchenAid Artisan Plus that currently sits on my countertop, you can gain extra functionality by connecting attachments to the central hub. While a separate food processor, like Cuisinart’s 14 Cup Custom Food Processor , is always a handy extra to have close by, KitchenAid’s stand mixer attachments let you slice, shred and spiralize vegetables, grind meat, make pasta, and even stuff sausages. If you’re looking to cut down on your countertop clutter, it makes sense to really think about how you work in your kitchen. If you don’t bake cookies and pies or make your own bread, you’d probably be better off with a food processor than a stand mixer. Artisan, 5-Qt Tilt Head Stand Mixer: was $499 now $349 The KitchenAid Artisan beats, whisks, and kneads at 10 speeds, and the bowl is big enough to mix 9 dozen cookies or 4 loaves of bread at a time. This machine also boasts a 59-point planetary mixing action — fancy words that translate into incredibly well-mixed ingredients. Plus, it includes a flat beater, a coated dough hook, a 6-wire whip, and a 1-piece pouring shield. The only problem you’ll have is choosing a color. View Deal 2. Air fryer (Image credit: Cosori) One of the best air fryers serves as an essential holiday backup when your turkey takes over your oven, and there’s no room left to roast potatoes or bake crispy puff-pastry appetizers. Of course, it all depends on the size of your main oven and whether you’re juggling a single or double cavity, but for me, that extra cooking space is a must when I’m hosting. There are other alternatives to using an air fryer — you could swap it for one of the best toaster ovens , a standard microwave , or even Ninja’s Crispi Microwave , which I recently tested and bridges the gap between a microwave and an air fryer. The catch is they all take up precious countertop space — probably more than a multi-functioning air fryer. How will I be using my air fryer over the holidays? While I frequently roast a whole chicken in my Cosori Turboblaze Air fryer , a turkey is unfortunately far too snug a fit! Instead, I'll be making the most of my air fryer to prove dough, cook stuffing balls and roast crispy potatoes. And as it acts like a mini convection oven, I might even try pumpkin pie. articles.title: Need a Netflix romance miniseries you can binge in a single weekend? I found 3 that will make you swoon, from a ‘Bridgerton’ prequel to a 100% Rotten Tomatoes gem
articles.content: When it comes to the miniseries format, we're used to high-tension genres like true crime , historical drama , psychological thrillers, and family sagas. Finding a short-form series dedicated to romance — where the stakes are more of the will-they-won't-they emotional sort — feels far rarer, but not impossible, as these three great Netflix miniseries prove. One of the best streaming services around, Netflix is packed with romantic miniseries you'll fall for, whether you're after a small-screen adaptation of a beloved romance book, a costume drama set in the greater " Bridgerton " universe, or a Christmas-season charmer full of lovely optimism and holiday cheer. And, even better, the critics agree — each of the following shows has an impressive 90% or higher rating on Rotten Tomatoes. If you're after a sweet, moving love story that plays out across a handful of episodes, here are five Netflix romance miniseries to add to your watchlist. 'One Day' Based on the bestselling 2009 romance novel by British author David Nicholls, " One Day " charts the slow-burn romance between University of Edinburgh grads Emma Morley and Dexter Mayhew — played by the winning duo of Ambika Mod and Leo Woodall, who share a wonderfully natural, palpable chemistry — over the course of two decades, catching up with the characters on the same date every year. Over 14 half-hour episodes, we see Emma and Dexter grow up, break up, make up, and try to find their respective places in the world, allowing for heavier things like loss, heartbreak, and healing in a genre that's usually smitten by the lighthearted and breezy. The romantic drama has a strong 92% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with critics showering particular praise on Mod and Woodall's lead performances. "Chronicling the passage of time with well-observed sweep, 'One Day' is by turns giddy and somber but always swooningly romantic," reads the site's critical consensus. Stream "One Day" on Netflix now 'Queen Charlotte: A Bridgerton Story' When it comes to Netflix romantic series, few names are bigger than " Bridgerton ," the streamer's Regency-era romance following the relationship entanglements and social pressures of the eight Bridgerton siblings . (The show will be back for its steamy fifth season next year.) But equally swoon-worthy is the "Bridgerton" miniseries " Queen Charlotte: A Bridgerton Story ," which serves as a prequel to the O.G. Netflix romance. The six-episode historical drama focuses on the 1761 arranged marriage of 17-year-old Princess Charlotte (a star-making breakthrough performance from India Amarteifio) to King George III (Corey Mylchreest), which kicks off an epic love story that changes the course of England. Mixing genuine emotional depth with sharp social commentary, "Queen Charlotte" is "a resplendent romance between two of the most interesting characters in the 'Bridgerton saga'" and "a spin-off that arguably perfects the primary series' formula," per the critical consensus on Rotten Tomatoes, where the miniseries has an excellent 94% approval rating. Stream "Queen Charlotte: A Bridgerton Story" on Netflix now 'Dash & Lily' Sure, it's not even Thanksgiving yet, but who says we can't get into the Christmas spirit a little early, right? This cheery 2020 rom-com series will help you do just that: Midori Francis ("Saccharine") and Austin Abrams — who has been a bit of a scream king lately, between 2025's "Weapons" and this year's "Resident Evil" —play two New York City teens who develop feelings for each other through traded messages in a shared red notebook, before they ever lay eyes on each other. Over eight episodes, the youngsters — she, a holiday optimist, and he, a bit of a Christmas Scrooge — challenge each other to step out of their comfort zones through written dares, personal thoughts, and revealed secrets, all set against iconic locations in snowy New York City. The romance series received the ever-so-rare 100% critical score on Rotten Tomatoes, with critics praising…

articles.title: Satellites Now Outnumber the Visible Stars Above Most Towns
articles.content: Satellites now outnumber visible stars in the night sky above many towns and cities, according to a non-peer-reviewed analysis by engineering firm Accu Components. The researchers estimated that roughly 710 satellites pass over an average U.K. town at any given moment, with about 105 illuminated by sunlight and potentially visible to the naked eye. Space.com reports: Although the researchers specifically focused on the U.K., they say that such heavy satellite traffic flows above most of Europe, the U.S. and other mid-latitude regions, especially between 40 and 50 degrees north or south. "Most Starlink satellites orbit at around 53 degrees to the equator, so the satellites bunch up over the mid-latitudes. These worldwide figures are approximate, based on a global grid over a single day," Accu Components spokesperson told Space.com in an email. "Skies near the equator are the quietest, with around 490 satellites." Not all of those satellites are visible to the naked eye, the researchers said in a statement. Because satellites unlike stars don't produce their own light, they must be illuminated by the sun, while the ground below has already sunk into darkness, to be visible. [...] The spokesperson said that the actual number of visible satellites varies drastically throughout the night. During the hours after dusk and before dawn, a much greater number of satellites can be seen, while in the middle of the night most no longer catch any light. "For a typical U.K. town, around 300 satellites are catching the sunlight in the first hour or so after dark," the spokesperson said. "That falls to fewer than 20 around midnight, then climbs back to around 300 before dawn." [...] The study found that throughout the night, an average U.K. town sees 12,891 different satellites passing overhead. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Google DeepMind Releases Gemini 4 Neon: 1M Context, #1 on AA Coding Agent Index
articles.content: Google DeepMind just released Gemini 4 Neon . Gemini 4 Neon is a reasoning model that sits between Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen. It targets coding agents, knowledge work and science workflows. The developer pitch is near-frontier scores at a lower cost per task. Pricing is $3 per 1M input tokens and $15 per 1M output tokens. TL;DR Size: 1M-token unified context, 64K default output, up to 1M via background long decode. Runs on: Google-hosted only. Closed weights, so no local GPU, quantized or edge builds. Performance: 61 on the AA Intelligence Index, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (59) and GPT-6.2 Sol (57). Best: 95.2% on GraphWalks (256K to 1M context), vs 80.1% for GPT-6.2 Sol. Worst: 46.2% on FrontierCode 2.0, behind Claude Opus 5.5 at 47.3%. Bottom line: Best: leads long-context and agentic coding at $3/$15. Worst: closed, self-reported, pricier per token than GPT-6.2 Sol. What is Gemini 4 Neon? Neon is the middle model in the Gemini 4 family. Carbon handles the hardest long-horizon projects. Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution. Neon balances depth and efficiency between the two. As per the model card , Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. Google does not disclose parameter count or architecture. Inputs cover text, images, audio and video. The knowledge cutoff is March 2026. How does Neon work inside agent workflows? Neon exposes multiple thinking levels. High is the default. xhigh is reserved for the hardest engineering, analytical and science workloads. For long agent runs, Neon supports context compaction and makes fewer redundant file reads. In Google Antigravity , Neon can act as an orchestrator. It directs parallel Gemini 4 Hydrogen subagents on smaller subtasks. How does Gemini 4 Neon perform on benchmarks? Google compares Neon against Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol. All scores below are reported by Google, not independently reproduced. Coding: #1 on the AA Coding Agent Index at 58.6. SWE-sweep with provider harness hits 39.0%, vs 10.1% for Opus 5.5. Knowledge work: 56.3% on Zapier AutomationBench , vs 42.5% for Opus 5.5. 75.8% on Agents’ Last Exam v1.1 . Science and reasoning: 84.0% on RiemannBench , 70.5% on Terminal-Bench-Science and 71.3% on HLE-Diamond . Long context: 95.2% on GraphWalks, vs 66.8% for Opus 5.5. Cyber: 90.5% on SEC-bench Pro , 70.7% on CWE-Bench v2 and 51.3% on WebExploitBench v1.2. Neon does not win every row. Opus 5.5 leads Terminal-bench 4.1 (65.8% vs 65.2%) and FrontierCode 2.0 (47.3% vs 46.2%). GPT-6.2 Sol leads Chartography (75.1% vs 73.5%). On the Vals Index , Neon scores 70.9% and ranks #2. On the Agent Arena index it also ranks #2, with a score of 1336. What does Gemini 4 Neon cost? Neon lists at $3 input, $0.15 cached input and $15 output per 1M tokens. Google says Neon at high thinking costs 32% less per task than Carbon. It also claims 50% to 80% lower cost per task vs rivals on Vals Index and Agent Arena. At xhigh, Google cites 36%+ lower cost than rivals at their highest settings. Those are per-task claims, not per-token prices. GPT-6.2 Sol lists at $2/$10. Claude Opus 5.5 lists at $4/$20. Gemini 4 Carbon is $2/$10 until November 30, then $4/$20. Where can developers use Gemini 4 Neon? Gemini API paid tier, via Google AI Studio and Android Studio Gemini for business , via API and the model dropdown Google Antigravity, for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers The Gemini app , for Pro and Ultra subscribers What do the safety numbers show? Neon runs on the Gemini 4 safety and security stack . Google reports a 0.09% misaligned action rate on its agentic safety suite. It passes 99.2% of the agent honesty evaluation. It shows a 0.0% attack success rate on Gray Swan’s prompt injection benchmark at the highest thinking level. Its 2.45% shortcut rate on a coding cheating test is the lowest of any Gemini 4 model. articles.title: GTA VI didn’t break the internet, thanks to ‘stupid DNS tricks’
articles.content: Grand Theft Auto VI may put a dent in global productivity today but the game didn’t break the internet. For those unfamiliar, GTA VI is the first new instalment of the mega-hit game in 13 years and it is nearly impossible to understate the excitement surrounding its release. Anecdotal evidence suggests fans of the game may today report they suddenly feel unfit to perform paid work. Developer Rockstar Games allowed Xbox and PlayStation owners to pay for and download the 200GB-plus game on November 10, before play commenced on the 19 th . Millions took advantage of the chance to download the game, creating just the sort of internet traffic event that regional internet registry the Réseaux IP Européens Network Coordination Centre (RIPE NCC) can observe with its RIPE Atlas internet measurement network. RIPE data scientist Emile Aben, with help from staffers Alun Davies and James Cowie, went looking for GTA-related traffic and found some interesting patterns . Aben observed that traffic to PlayStations mostly came from content delivery networks operated by AWS and Fastly. Microsoft relied on Fastly for over half of traffic flowing to Xboxes and used Akamai too, but eschewed AWS's CloudFront. The data scientist observed heavy use of “GeoDNS,” a technique that returns different IP addresses for a single domain request, depending on a user’s location. DNS’s designers didn’t intend that. Indeed, the RIPE trio point out that Paul Vixie, the computer scientist who earned his place in the Internet Hall of Fame for massive contributions to the DNS system, regarded things like GeoDNS as “stupid DNS tricks.” Whatever you think of GeoDNS, the RIPE researchers found that folks who were likely downloading GTA VI from Los Angeles, Tokyo, and Istanbul were each directed to different sites. Their probe of a network in Shanghai, China, found “a very distinct long lookup-chain with a hostname that is associated with the Alibaba Cloud in the end that maps to six different IP addresses.” “This hints at specialised treatment for some countries/regions,” Aben wrote. He also noted that Internet Exchange Points, the interconnect facilities that network operators use to exchange traffic and shorten paths, had to cope with record traffic during the download period – and seem to have handled the load. Aben thinks the GTA VI download program offers a useful lesson. “DNS helps steer each player towards a download server, while multiple CDNs share the work of delivering the files,” he wrote. “That distribution matters beyond gaming. On the open Internet, game downloads share routers and link capacity with all kinds of other traffic, including critical services.” “Keeping downloads local helps leave capacity on long-distance links free for other uses, making that enormous demand manageable.” ®

articles.title: Replit’s CEO on its stunning turnaround, ‘AI psychosis,’ and the risk Silicon Valley is ignoring
articles.content: A couple of years ago, Replit was flatlining at a few million dollars in annual revenue and running a mostly empty office after a layoff. Today the vibe coding pioneer is valued at $9 billion, up from $3 billion just six months ago. CEO Amjad Masad reveals what made the turnaround possible. Masad also weighs in on what he calls “ AI psychosis,” and says cybersecurity, not AI extinction, is the risk worth focusing on. This is an abridged transcript of an interview from Rapid Response , recorded live at Masters of Scale Summit 2026 and hosted by former Fast Company editor-in-chief Robert Safian. From the team behind the Masters of Scale podcast, Rapid Response features candid conversations with today’s top business leaders navigating real-time challenges. Subscribe to Rapid Response wherever you get your podcasts to ensure you never miss an episode. The growth you’ve seen has been extraordinary. From the inside, what does that feel like? Is it exhilarating when everything is growing so fast? Is it terrifying? Do you have to pinch yourself to say, “Is this real?” It’s all of the above. The first feeling I had was a little bit of vindication, because I started talking about everyone being able to code and create software back in 2010, when I was building the kind of precursor to Replit as an open-source project. Then I was a founding engineer at Codecademy, where we taught a lot of people to code. And when we started Replit in 2016, we were like, “We want to blur this distinction between learning to code and doing code, and build an environment that really makes it so that anyone with an idea can build software.” And for a long time, people didn’t believe us. Raising capital was hard. Recruiting people was hard. Because some of the technology wasn’t ready yet. It wasn’t ready. It was on track, and I could see it happening. There were many moments where the company could have died, or I could have quit. It would have been very easy to quit at many different moments. And so in 2024, when we invented what would later be called vibe coding, when we came up with the first fully natural-language-based programming environment, there was nothing out there at the time. People really appreciated it, and we started seeing these stories of people having ideas. One of the early experiences I had was someone recording a video of themselves and posting it on Twitter and YouTube where they were crying because they had this idea of overlaying all their memories and their photos on a map and being able to explore their life through this map. It’s a simple idea, but it’s a personal app. It’s not even a commercial app. And he was crying because he said he had this idea for so long. He tried to do it with all these different technologies, and for the first time, he was able to do it. I’ve also been an angel investor for a while, and I’ve seen some early AI companies do the hypergrowth and the hyper-deceleration within a year. So there’s a fair amount of paranoia built into how we operate. You immigrated to the U.S. in 2012, and as you say, you spent years grinding away as you were trying to find your groove. Are there lessons from those slower times that you go back to as a leader in the midst of the noise you’re in now? Yeah. There were many moments where it felt darkest just before we were able to invent something big or new. Even just before we invented agentic coding in 2024, we had to do a layoff. We were six or seven years into the company, we had 2 or 3 million in ARR, and it was flatlining. It wasn’t growing at all. Two or three million? Yeah. Two or three million, just a couple of years ago. Now you’re at a billion. Yeah. I want to pause and acknowledge that. That’s crazy, man. It is wild. And we were burning a ton of money. We hired a great team, but the future hadn’t arrived as fast as I thought it would. So I kind of…

articles.title: How to use NotProton to unlock Windows game compatibility in Steam for Mac
articles.content: NotProton lets Mac owners install and play Windows games through the native Steam client without installing Windows. Here's how to set it up and what worked on our M3 MacBook Air . Running Windows games on Mac Steam for Mac normally won't let you install Windows-only games, but NotProton offers a way around that limitation. We used it to launch two Windows games, including a 3D title whose Mac version no longer works on modern macOS releases. Both games launched with functioning graphics, audio, and controls, although one eventually froze. Getting everything running also required some troubleshooting with CrossOver and macOS permissions. NotProton brings Steam Play functionality to the native macOS Steam client, allowing Mac owners to install and launch Windows games through compatibility software. articles.title: South Korea tries to out exam cheats with Extreme Emergency smartphone alert
articles.content: At 08:30 on Thursday morning every powered-on mobile phone in South Korea blared out an Extreme Emergency Alert tone for 10.5 seconds – but the nation was at peace, with no major natural disasters occurring. The extreme emergency South Korea hoped to avoid was cheating in the annual College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), an exam that over half a million people sit in the hope of securing admission to their preferred university. This year, around a third of those applicants are repeating the test after their previous effort didn’t get them the result they wanted. CSAT involves five separate examinations staged in a single day. Participants can only bring pencils to the test. Smartphones or any sort of tech is strictly forbidden. Which is why Korean authorities used the national alert system on the day of CSAT, because if the 40dB tone sounded in an exam centre, it could indicate a student had deliberately or inadvertently tried to bring a smartphone – perhaps as an exam aide. Korean media report the 08:30 alert turned up nine phones. Authorities will send a second alert tone at an unspecified time later in the day to again smoke out any surreptitious smartphones. It’s not possible to opt out of the alerts, one reason a concerned netizen has used the Android issue tracker to suggest sending alerts to detect exam cheats could be an abuse of the emergency alert system that Google might want to do something about. South Korea sends a lot of emergency alerts, for matters such as helping to find missing persons or to warn of dangerous weather. It’s not uncommon to receive several in a single day. Authorities also gave advance notice of the CSAT alerts, which will not, therefore, cause panic on the streets of Seoul or Busan. CSAT day is, however, a serious occasion. Some businesses open late so test-takers can get to their exams without having to battle peak hour traffic. Those measures are arguably less disruptive than the widespread internet outages that some states in India impose on major exam days. An alleged leak of one Indian exam paper saw the nation’s tech regulator ban messaging service Telegram in the country and eventually sparked a youth protest movement that New Delhi tried to suppress with more deliberate internet outages. ®
articles.author: Simon Sharwood

articles.title: New Study Shows How Young People Feel About AI Companions
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from 404 Media: A new study from Gallup looked at how young people across the world are making friends, both digitally and in person. The good news is that around 93% of the young people surveyed reported having at least one strong in-person friendship. The weird news is that 33% said they had an AI companion. Gallup's study is lengthy and nuanced. It partnered with the Boston Children's Digital Wellness Lab to conduct the study and used online surveys of more than 16,000 young people from the ages of 15 to 22 in 16 different countries. A lot of the topline results won't surprise anyone living in today's constantly online digital-forward age. Gallup found that respondents felt their in-person friendships were their strongest, that digital friendships complemented rather than replaced in-person ones, and that stronger friendships made people happier no matter how the connection was made. Three things that stood out were how the young respondents talked about AI, loneliness, and doomscrolling. Young people in the United States, Canada, and UK reported the least interest in AI overall, with only 20% saying they used it once a day or more. Almost 40 percent of young people in Brazil use it daily. Japan and Italy both come in around 35%. "Nearly half of young people in the United States, United Kingdom and Canada have used AI no more than a few times in the past month, including those who have not used it at all," the researchers wrote. Most of the respondents (82%) said they'd used AI to look up information, 68% asked it for advice, and 33% used it as a companion. Young people with online-only friends were more likely to use AI for companionship, "although these patterns do not establish whether AI companionship supplements or substitutes for human relationships," they wrote. The researchers discovered that people in different countries felt wildly different about their AI buddies. Almost half of Australians with AI friends rated the relationship as "high quality" and only 12% of young people in Poland did. Mostly, though, people thought of their AI friends as mid: "In most countries [...] young people are more likely to give their AI companionship a medium rating than either a high or low rating." People who used AI as a friend also reported higher levels of loneliness, the study found. "However, the findings cannot determine whether young people turn to AI because they feel lonely, whether AI companionship influences their social experiences or whether other circumstances help explain these relationships," the researchers wrote. [...] The study's authors warned about reading too much into these results. "These assessments should be compared cautiously with those for human friendships examined in this report, as young people may have different expectations of what makes an AI companion or human friendship meaningful or supportive," the researchers wrote. "The broader message is not that one form of connection is inherently better or worse, but that the quality of young people's relationships and the wider social context in which they exist matter greatly," the study concluded. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Nutrient Data Extraction API: JSON Matching Your Schema With Per-Field Citations and Confidence
articles.content: An LLM presents you a wrong value extracted from a document as fact. That error is costly, especially when basing decisions on it. The Nutrient Data Extraction API targets that problem. It parses PDFs, scans, images and Office files into spatial JSON or Markdown. Extract maps fields from a document onto your JSON schema, and split, classify and form endpoints provide useful primitives for your document pipelines. Each extracted value is anchored to a page via a bounding box, a match label and a confidence score. Nutrient (formerly PSPDFKit) runs the same engine behind an MCP server , agent skill, Mac app and SDK . TL;DR Size: A hosted API with 4 parse modes plus auto routing. Runs on: Nutrient cloud, your own servers via SDK, or an Apple silicon Mac. Where to try it: Studio , a browser workspace to configure and test parsing, extraction,classification, splitting, and form filling. Performance: 86.2 overall on Nutrient’s WholeDoc Bench , top of 19 settings (live API, Agentic). Best: 86.2 at 1.8¢ per page, versus 67.1 at 17.8¢ for the best frontier-model setting. How do you test it in Studio before writing code? Studio is Nutrient’s browser workspace for configuring and testing the API before integrating it in your application. It enables you to test parsing, extraction, classification , splitting, and form filling on your own files. A typical loop: Upload a sample document and set the parameters you plan to send. Draft a schema in the UI, or generate one based on your own documents. Run it on a fresh document, then inspect values and citations. Save the setup as a versioned preset. The API calls it a processor , with a proc_ ID. Score preset versions against up to 25 reviewed documents in an evaluation set. Processors saved in Studio can then be called from the API by ID. Which mode should you pick? Auto routes each page to structure , understand or agentic . If the mode is omitted, the API defaults to understand . Operation Best for Price per page Extract per page WholeDoc Bench* Parse: text Born-digital PDFs and Office files, no OCR $0.001 $0.007** Not tested Parse: structure OCR for scans with simple layouts, no AI $0.0015 $0.0075 39.4 Parse: understand AI layout analysis: forms, complex layouts $0.009 $0.015 80.8 Parse: agentic Vision language model: cursive, degraded scans, charts $0.018 $0.024 86.2 Classify Zero-shot document labels $0.001 n/a n/a Split Separating merged PDFs into documents $0.003 n/a n/a * WholeDoc Bench parsing score, 5 November 2026; not extraction accuracy. Extract adds $0.006 per page. **API docs list text-mode extract; the agent skill starts at structure. Pricing is in dollars, from 1 balance shared across Nutrient’s cloud APIs, so teams can mix and match. The free plan gives you $5 monthly usage that covers about 330 understand-mode extractions. Starter costs $75 a month for $90 of usage; Growth costs $275 for $345. How does grounded confidence work? In Nutrient’s confidence post , a field scored 0.97 but came from the wrong column. The current score is a composite of optional signals: token probability, candidate margin, grounding and format. Nutrient’s NLI grounding model is open under Apache-2.0. A grounded value can still answer the wrong field. When no score exists, confidence is omitted, not low. Each field also gets a match label: id_match, id_match_multiblock, id_match_partial, fuzzy_match or not_found. Gate on the label first, then confidence. articles.title: Why Groundcover’s CEO says agents are the power users of observability
articles.content: An AI coding agent can write a patch in minutes. Ask it whether that patch slows down the API endpoint your customers hit most, and suddenly it needs something that lives outside the repository. It needs to see how the software runs. That’s the premise behind Groundcover , an observability platform that wants to put production telemetry in the hands of developers and their coding agents. Yes, you read that correctly. In a conversation with The New Stack ’s Frederic Lardinois at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon this month in Salt Lake City, Groundcover CEO and co-founder Shahar Azulay explained why he thinks the same data engineers use to troubleshoot an incident can help an agent write and test a better change in the first place. Your new observability user is an agent “Now agents are the power users of observability,” Azulay told TNS. Groundcover exposes telemetry through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) , giving coding agents a way to query it while they work. An agent investigating a slow API, for example, could use traces to see which service accounts for most of the latency. A developer writing a test could use observed application behavior to pick a scenario customers actually encounter. Groundcover uses that approach internally. Its coding agents pull context from the company’s own telemetry, and agents involved in code review can look at measurements from staging deployments. It’s a way to give a reviewer something concrete to check when a patch looks perfectly reasonable in a diff. Agents also give engineers something new to monitor. Azulay contrasts a familiar application trace that follows a request across several microservices with an agent run that can span hours and thousands of tool calls. A trace that long can make a Kubernetes incident look like light reading. Developers may need to inspect prompts and tool calls or use evaluations to judge whether a run behaved as intended. A completed run tells you the agent stopped. The trace can help you figure out what it did along the way. Less instrumentation work, more room for detail Groundcover uses an eBPF sensor to collect application and infrastructure telemetry without requiring developers to add an SDK to every service. It also supports OpenTelemetry, so teams can keep sending the signals they already collect and add custom instrumentation where they need more detail. That gives developers a baseline for a new service and a way to get more specific when a particular path or business operation warrants it. Where the data runs is part of the pitch. Groundcover’s bring-your-own-cloud model keeps telemetry and Groundcover’s agent operations in the customer’s cloud environment, Azulay said. Customers pay for the underlying infrastructure, and Groundcover manages the deployment. For teams weighing how much telemetry to retain, the model puts the infrastructure bill in their own account. It also matters when prompts or tool calls may contain sensitive customer data and teams want to keep that information under their control. We also ask what happens when the platform starts acting on what it sees. Azulay points to Groundcover’s move into Kubernetes optimization, where the immediate work centers on cost and resilience. He sees a path from there to agents that can help address an incident on both sides of the deployment, proposing a code change and adjusting infrastructure configuration. The conversation also gets into the practical work of switching observability platforms, including what happens to the dashboards and monitors engineers have spent years building. Watch the full KubeCon interview on The New Stack ’s YouTube channel to hear how Groundcover uses its own telemetry in code reviews and why Azulay thinks the next generation of coding agents will be a regular part of the observability stack. articles.title: Microsoft brings AI inference closer to enterprise data with Windows Server 2028
articles.content: Microsoft is betting on a hybrid future where AI inferencing takes place where it makes the most sense. Which, logically, is where data already lives: On enterprise-controlled infrastructure. To that end, this week at Microsoft Ignite , the tech giant announced Windows Server 2028, its largest platform update since Windows Server 2025. Now in public preview, the next generation server is positioned as a foundation for AI inference that supports “enterprise hybrid intelligence.” It introduces new AI accelerators so enterprises can run inference on their own infrastructure, storage tools for accelerated data transfer, security controls to establish a “secure baseline from day one,” and simplified admin and management dashboards. But while it promises new capabilities across automation, management, identity, security, recovery, storage, and virtualization, it’s still early days for Windows Server 2028, with various features at different levels of availability and maturity. “It’s important to remember that this is the public preview phase, so a lot still remains a promise on the roadmap,” noted Infotech associate VP John Annand . Supporting enterprises where they are Windows Server 2028 gives customers the ability to run inferencing workloads close to physical operations and in their own controlled ecosystems. This means they don’t have to build and operate a “separate AI stack for every location,” Windows Server product team leader Neil Hinnant explained in a blog post . Microsoft is introducing AI accelerators in its servers; notably, AMD’s Instinct MI350P card is be in preview in the first half of 2027 for supported Windows Server systems, including Server 2028. The company is also developing tools to manage that hardware, deploy and configure inference environments , and direct model requests to appropriate environments. Microsoft said the offering also begins its long-term investments to extend Microsoft Foundry to “fleets of local token factories,” and to support open-weight and custom models across Foundry Local, Windows ML, vLLM, and Llama.cpp. “As AI-accelerated workloads diffuse across the enterprise, different workloads have different needs,” Hinnant wrote. “Cost, latency, IP protection, data residency, and regulatory requirements all shape that decision.” New security, storage, admin features From a security standpoint, Windows Server 2028 has a hardened Server Core configuration “by default,” with hundreds of security settings enabled on first boot, aligned with industry benchmarks. “The secure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup,” Microsoft explained . Enterprises need only relax the settings their workloads need. “That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened.” The new server incorporates a containment layer for isolation, Agent 365 for agent identity and governance, and virtual machine (VM) protection to build a chain of trust. Microsoft says it is also investing in automatic certificate management to verify both human and machine identities, prevent compromise, and encrypt traffic, alongside post-quantum cryptography. This can balance day-to-day security tasks with longer term needs to modernize “against the threats of tomorrow.” Also by default, Windows Server 2028 supports native non-volatile memory express (NVMe) storage to “give demanding workloads more room to grow.” Enterprises need to be able to apply policy, manage updates, and get a view of what’s running across their estates. Intune management for Windows Servers, now in preview, brings endpoint management workflows including configuration, compliance, and updates to eligible and always-on servers. articles.title: GTA VI gamers beware — experts warn of a 1300% rise in phishing scams ahead of official launch date
articles.content: A 1,300% surge in gaming-related phishing emails has been detected, with interest in GTA VI cited as the driving force 42.4% of all phishing email attempts at the end of October 2026 were GTA-related impersonation attempts Cybercriminals are using fake GTA VI pre-order offers to fool employees into handing over credentials for “workplace benefits” Organizations are being urged to crack down on GTA VI-related emails and communications, following a striking uptick in phishing emails related to the upcoming video game. Following an increase of 1,300%, gaming-related phishing emails appear to be big business for scammers right now, with GTA VI the lure in the majority of cases. Fake workplace bonuses, employee benefits, and QR codes holding “discounts” are all part of this wave of corporate phishing attacks, with 35% of similar attacks targeting the UK. Only the US, with 47% of attacks, has attracted more attention from the GTA VI scammers. While security filtering software should be updated, employees should be vigilant, and made aware of the personal and corporate risks of falling for the dual attack strategy. GTA-themed corporate phishing The attempts to fool would-be victims with one eye on the release date of the most anticipated video game of all time rely on what is being termed “GTA-themed phishing.” Two main waves are being employed: Wave 1, the mass-market email lure that is designed to overwhelm detection provisions and draw victims to anonymous landing pages with fake Rockstar Games branding, and Wave 2. This second phrase is a smarter approach, targeting enterprise systems over the weekend, offering free or discounted pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6. It claims to be from the employer and relies on artificial urgency (e.g. the first 250 employees, expires in 48 hours, etc.) to fool recipients. Once hooked in, the targets are redirected to fraudulent online casinos, and have their credentials harvested. Dual-wave attack These “dual-wave… hype-driven attacks” are designed to exploit the targets as much as possible. With this in mind, cybersecurity advice outfit KnowBe4 is recommending what is described as a “layered defense strategy.” This includes training employees to recognize lures such as fake HR perks, and understanding their correct context – legitimate perks appear on company intranets, rather than being sent as unsolicited messages that include external links. They note: “To ensure these targeted corporate lures bypass perimeter defenses, attackers combine psychological manipulation with a multi-layered technical evasion strategy. Rather than spoofing existing brands, threat actors register look-alike vendor domains that allow their emails to cleanly pass SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication checks. Once inside the inbox, the messages evade traditional image-based scanners by rendering QR codes entirely out of Unicode text block characters or HTML tables.“ So, stronger internal messaging, such as reminding teams that company benefits don’t rely on artificial urgency or QR codes is recommended. Limiting employees’ ability to use QR codes and minimize “quishing” where the device shift strategy – which bypasses corporate security measures – is also a smart precaution.

articles.title: Instagram Now Lets You Save Songs to Apple Music
articles.content: Sometime in the last week or two , Instagram added a new Apple Music feature. You can now connect an ‌Apple Music‌ account to the social network and save songs you come across to an ‌Apple Music‌ playlist. If you tap a song link on a post or a story on Instagram, you'll see a prompt to connect Instagram to ‌Apple Music‌. Once your ‌Apple Music‌ account is linked to Instagram, you can tap a song name in a post and use the "Add to ‌Apple Music‌" button to save it. Songs are saved in an "Instagram Songs" playlist in the Library section of the Music app. Instagram previously supported sharing ‌Apple Music‌ songs in Stories and direct messages, but there was no option for saving content from Instagram to ‌Apple Music‌. Spotify also supports saving songs from Instagram to the Liked Songs section on the streaming service. articles.title: China goes public with stealth UAV manned by crack team of 'self-trained female drone operators' — GJ-11 looks a lot like Northrop Grumman's X-47B now-defunct UCAV
articles.content: New footage exposes the GJ-11's internal weapons bays and stealth-focused design China identifies airstrikes and enemy air defense suppression as planned missions Retractable landing gear and nose sensors emerge in newly released footage China has released television footage of its GJ-11 stealth combat drone, revealing previously unseen structural details and operational activities. The broadcast exposed the aircraft's internal weapons compartments, landing gear, nose-mounted sensors, and distinctive exhaust arrangement. The Chinese military says this stealth combat drone is designed for airstrikes and Suppression of Enemy Air Defenses (SEAD), among other intended missions GJ-11 reveals internal weapons bays The GJ-11 has two internal weapons compartments beneath its fuselage, each protected by separately operated doors with serrated edges. Its precise dimensions remain unknown, but available footage suggests they could accommodate weapons weighing approximately 1,000 to 2,000 pounds. Chinese state television reported that the compartments support different air-to-ground and surface-attack munitions. Its internal carriage allows the aircraft to transport weapons without external mounting equipment, which could compromise its aerodynamic performance and increase radar detectability. The newly released sequences also showed the landing gear retracting after takeoff, revealing a substantial arrangement featuring a twin-wheel nose assembly. Another important feature is a trapezoidal installation beneath the nose, apparently housing electro-optical and infrared sensors for observation and targeting operations. Similar installations appear on China's J-20 and J-35 fighters, although the actual capabilities and configuration of the GJ-11's equipment remain undisclosed. At the rear, the aircraft features a flattened exhaust outlet integrated into its upper fuselage, with the engine intake located above the main airframe. These arrangements are intended to reduce radar and infrared signatures, complementing the aircraft's tailless flying-wing configuration and internally carried weapons. Airstrikes and cooperation with J-16 and J-20 fighters SEAD missions require aircraft to locate, disrupt, or destroy hostile radar installations and missile systems protecting defended airspace. The GJ-11's stealth configuration and internal weapons compartments could allow it to approach these defenses while carrying weapons for precision attacks. The broadcast also showed mission planning involving GJ-11 aircraft operating alongside J-16 multirole fighters and J-20 fifth-generation stealth aircraft. These arrangements suggest that China intends to employ the uncrewed platform alongside crewed aircraft for reconnaissance, weapons delivery and other combat responsibilities. However, the footage does not explain how targeting information moves between participating aircraft or establish the GJ-11's available autonomous capabilities. The aircraft's development traces back to the experimental Sharp Sword demonstrator before the GJ-11 appeared publicly during China's October 2019 military parade. Satellite imagery subsequently recorded repeated testing at Malan in Xinjiang, while three examples reportedly appeared at Shigatse in Tibet between August and September 2025. The GJ-11 resembles Northrop Grumman's X-47B in its flying-wing shape, stealth design and internal weapons compartments, although the American aircraft never entered active military service or operational combat. Via TWZ
articles.author: Efosa Udinmwen

articles.title: Owning an Apple Home: Bye bye SwitchBot
articles.content: After months of living with various SwitchBot products, namely the Lock Vision Pro and garage door opener, I've finally given up and ripped all SwitchBot products from my Apple Home . Here's why. SwitchBot is no longer working for me In July, I wrote a story for the "Owning an Apple Home" column specifically on the Broken Promise of Matter . That story was directly inspired by my frustrating experience installing and using SwitchBot products in my Apple Home. Just four months later, I've removed every SwitchBot product from Apple Home, disconnected them from power, and put them away. Things were rough at the start, but conditions began deteriorating in the last few weeks, and before anyone suggests it, before beta software or new Apple TV hardware was introduced. articles.title: Google’s Gemini 4 Neon tripled its coding score without changing the model
articles.content: Google’s new Gemini 4 Neon resolved 12.8% of the SWE-sweep coding benchmark using the mini-SWE harness, but that score jumped to 39.0% when the same model ran inside Antigravity . The more-than-threefold improvement raises questions about how much coding-agent performance comes from the underlying model and how much depends on the harness… Both results were reported Wednesday as part of the Neon launch. The more-than-threefold improvement raises questions about how much coding-agent performance comes from the underlying model and how much depends on the harness managing its tools, context, and execution. A day earlier, a FrontierHarness benchmark found that running the same open model could cost up to five times more depending on the harness Same model, different scores Google’s Gemini 4 Neon model card compares three frontier models on SWE-sweep using their respective provider harnesses and a shared mini-SWE baseline. Neon and Opus performed substantially better with their providers’ harnesses, but Sol did not. Claude Opus 5.5 climbed from 3.6% with mini-SWE to 10.1% with Claude Code, while GPT-6.2 Sol went the other way, falling from 11.6% with mini-SWE to 8.3% with Codex. Neon and Opus performed substantially better with their providers’ harnesses, but Sol did not. Google tested each model in two harness configurations, though the comparison does not isolate which changes account for the differences or whether the results would hold up across other benchmarks and repositories. The harness does the work Antigravity’s harness was co-trained with Gemini, and Neon has been updated to make fewer unnecessary file reads and better manage context during long coding sessions. Antigravity can also run subagents in separate Git worktrees and verify their changes. Google only tested Neon against mini-SWE, so there’s no data yet on how it performs with other harnesses. It’s unclear which of those changes contributed most to the SWE-sweep improvement, since they weren’t tested separately. Google only tested Neon against mini-SWE, so there’s no data yet on how it performs with other harnesses. Neon plans, Hydrogen builds Neon is joining the model-switching system Google introduced with Gemini 4 Hydrogen . It handles planning and harder coding problems, leaving routine work to Hydrogen, and can run multiple Hydrogen subagents in parallel using the /swarm feature introduced with Carbon . Google hasn’t said how much this setup affects Neon’s SWE-sweep results or what it means for the cost of completing a task. Counting the cost per task The company reports that Neon scored 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and 46.2% on FrontierCode 2.0 at its default high reasoning setting. It also topped the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with a score of 58.6. At its default high thinking level, the model costs 32% less per task than Gemini 4 Carbon, according to Google’s comparison using the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. API pricing is $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with cached input at $0.15 per million tokens and a 1 million-token context window. Neon is available through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and Gemini for Business. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can also access it through Antigravity. The post Google’s Gemini 4 Neon tripled its coding score without changing the model appeared first on The New Stack .
