articles.title: Chinese web giant Tencent says new US GPU ban ‘sets everyone back in China’
articles.content: The USA’s new ban on Chinese companies remotely accessing GPUs will have short-term impact, but ultimately see China accelerate its development of domestic alternatives, according to Martin Lau, the president of Chinese web giant Tencent. Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Lau said the new US regulation will have an “unfortunate” impact on Tencent’s business. “It does set everyone back. It sets everyone back in China,” Lau said. “So everyone is actually having less advanced compute to work with, no matter when you actually started leasing or building capacities outside of China.” He said the ban will impact Tencent’s ability to train models. “Our training efficiency with Hy4 is actually very high,” he said. “When we look at the next version, it would take probably longer time for us to come up with the next version in the short run.” “But over time, the domestic supply chain would actually come on board.” Lau also thinks the bans won’t hamper Tencent’s ability to run inferencing workloads, because made-in-China chips “should be able to cover it.” “And over the longer run, we believe all Chinese players would actually have to rely on domestic supply chains and domestic chips, which we see the industry is progressing very fast,” he added. “With the latest restriction, we expect it to actually speed up even further, because all the development effort would actually have to be focused on speeding up the domestic supply chain.” Tencent needs GPUs, and lots of them, because the 10 million users of its agentic assistant WorkBuddy are collectively consuming over 100 trillion tokens per day. Lau thinks WorkBuddy is on track to becoming a hit product, partly because many users are outside China. Lau said Tencent can serve WorkBuddy customers outside China because the service can operate with different models, and the company thinks it can find third parties to provide the necessary inferencing services without the new US bans creating a problem. But Lau said that GPU rentals and other cloud services, which are also growing strongly, may be impacted. “In terms of cloud, if it is non-GPU related, we can actually build capacities ourselves outside of China,” he said. “I think there is still a lot of such opportunities because our cloud service is actually very cost competitive. When it comes to GPU, then unfortunately, we cannot actually offer high-end GPU anymore. We may be able to work with some partners in different places.” Tencent doesn’t break out revenue for its cloud services, but said they rose by 35 percent year-on-year, well ahead of the company’s overall eight percent growth. Marketing services also grew strongly, by 19 percent, thanks in part to new AI-powered systems that improve ad targeting. The company’s WeChat and Weixin messaging platforms continued to grow, adding 35 million accounts to exiting the quarter with 1.44 billion monthly active users. One Tencent biz that went backwards was its international gaming unit, which saw revenue fall nine percent. Chief strategy officer James Mitchell said that slowdown wasn’t caused by the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. “ I think that in fairness, the slowdown for us predated the run-up to GTA VI,” he said, before predicting that Tencent’s existing and future “evergreen games” should help to turn things around. GPUs might help, too. “The game environment globally is one where the rate of innovation has slowed somewhat, and now with AI, there’s opportunities to re-accelerate innovation,” he said. ®

articles.title: This GMKtec Ryzen-powered mini PC is a solid daily driver with an $80 discount ahead of Black Friday
articles.content: The sheer efficiency of modern components means that you can get plenty of computing power inside a tiny chassis - and the GMKtec NucBox M6 is a good example of this. The system measures just 5.07 x 5 x 1.88 inches and weighs only 1.1 pounds, but it still packs a six-core AMD processor and serious expansion potential. And, thanks to an early Black Friday sale, it currently costs $499.99 after being reduced from $579.99. Today’s best GMKtec M6 Ultra deal M6 Ultra: was $579.99 now $499.99 The $499.99 configuration includes 16GB of DDR5 RAM and a 512GB SSD, with an $80 saving available directly from GMKtec. If you’d like a model with 32GB of memory and a 1TB SSD - ideal for tougher work scenarios - then its original price of $749.99 has been reduced to $679.99. For those who want a barebones rig, expect to pay $269.99 rather than $399.99. View Deal Why we recommend the GMKtec M6 Ultra The Ryzen 5 7640HS processor has six cores, 12 threads, and a boost speed of 5GHz. It also includes a Radeon 760M integrated graphics chip. It’s well suited to office work, multitasking and lighter gaming - think titles like Fortnite or League of Legends. It won’t handle tougher, high-end games, and the processor doesn’t have the power for heavier tasks like analyzing large data sets or tackling software development. There’s room to upgrade, too. Two DDR5 memory slots support up to 128GB RAM, even if you have to remove the original memory to deploy an effective upgrade, and the system has two M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 SSD slots that support up to 8TB of storage per slot. USB4, Wi-Fi 6E and dual 2.5Gb Ethernet provide plenty of connectivity. The main limitation is its integrated graphics, which won’t deliver the performance needed for demanding games. Price context and historical value At $499.99, the M6 Ultra is available with an $80 discount against its displayed price. That’s around a 14% discount. That’s better than the approximately 9% price drop that GMKtec is offering on the 32GB model right now. Should you buy it? ✅ Buy it if… your next mini PC needs to handle everyday computing and esports. ❌ Skip it if… you need serious gaming performance or the computing power for tough workloads.

articles.title: Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) on SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization
articles.content: Fine-tuning is the process of continuing to train a pretrained large language model (LLM) on a company’s own data so it adapts to a specific domain, task, or style rather than relying on general-purpose knowledge alone. For businesses, the value is twofold. A fine-tuned model delivers measurably better accuracy on domain-specific work while reducing costs: a smaller specialized model can match or exceed a frontier model on your task at a fraction of the per-token inference price. Those savings compound across millions of requests. Fine-tuning has therefore become an essential process for businesses looking to get more value from LLMs at lower costs. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods like Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) have emerged as a practical solution for fine-tuning LLMs to downstream tasks, reducing GPU capacity requirements by updating only a small subset of LLM parameters. LoRA aims to strike a balance between efficiency and expressiveness, however, the low-rank nature of the weight update inherently limits the representation power of LoRA fine-tuned models, potentially compromising performance on complex tasks. This trade-off hampers the ability of LoRA methods to capture complex patterns needed for diverse tasks. To address these challenges, Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) updates model parameters simultaneously, overcoming the low-rank limitations so LLMs can fully absorb complex domain-specific knowledge. Amazon SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization now supports Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) , so you can achieve superior model quality without managing infrastructure. There is no GPU provisioning, cluster setup, or distributed-training configuration required. In this post, we explore when and where FFT consistently outperforms LoRA across key benchmarks, examine the spectral properties of model weight matrices that explain this quality gap, provide practical hyperparameter tuning guidelines backed by controlled experiments using SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization, and show you how to get started with FFT on SageMaker AI. Full Fine-Tuning: Why it matters Model customization types like LoRA reduce trainable parameters by freezing the pre-trained model’s weights and injecting small, separate pairs of replacement matrices (called low-rank matrices) into the model layers. This works well for simple adaptations, but the low-rank structure inherently limits the representation power of the fine-tuned model. As tasks grow more complex and datasets scale beyond tens of thousands of examples, LoRA hits an accuracy plateau where increasing rank (and thus trainable parameters) fails to bridge the accuracy gap with standard fine-tuning. This plateau reveals that the performance gap isn’t simply because of fewer parameters. It’s caused by rank deficiency itself. The low-rank update can’t capture the full complexity of the weight changes needed for deep task adaptation. However, for complex tasks and domains where large, good-quality datasets exist, full-rank fine-tuning excels by updating model parameters simultaneously. FFT modifies the model’s weight matrix uniformly, using the full representational capacity of the model’s weight matrices rather than restricting updates to a small subspace, and without introducing the abrupt, localized distortions characteristic of low-rank methods. The result is stronger model convergence, better activation alignment across model layers, and a model that faithfully captures both the target task distribution and the richness of its pre-trained knowledge. FFT’s quality advantage grows with dataset scale: at 100K+ training examples, FFT achieved 90.0 percent on LLM-as-Judge semantic correctness across code generation tasks, as shown in the following chart. articles.title: Exa boosts embedding throughput by 50% to index billions of documents on AWS AI chips
articles.content: At Exa , we are building one of the few true web indexes by aggregating and serving knowledge from across the web, along with private and synthetic sources. We optimize the index for semantic search, grounding agents and humans in true, high-quality data. We use multi-tower semantic machine learning (ML) models to embed web data and query data into the same vector space, so users can express complex queries in natural language alongside traditional keyword search. The keystone technology behind this is an in-house vector database. It must ingest as much high-quality web data as possible and embed all of it. The unit economics of embedding therefore underlie everything we do. At the scale of tens or hundreds of billions of documents, finding the hardware that delivers the best performance per dollar isn’t a tuning detail. Any per-document cost improvement compounds into a significant number. This post details how we optimized our embedding infrastructure for cheaper, more flexible inference workloads on AWS Neuron hardware ( AWS Inferentia2 and AWS Trainium2 ), and how an agentic development workflow drove the optimization. Inference runs on an asynchronous pipeline, but it must be high-volume and fast to serve recent data quickly and shrink the time between discovery and serving. Figure 1: A simplified view of the Exa stack Every structured web document we rank as high enough quality must be embedded before it can be served. This figure shows how raw web data moves from Crawlers into an asynchronous pipeline of Parse, Moderate and filter, then Embed, with the result served from a vector database. Embedding documents at scale Our experience with the Neuron hardware family began with a backfill. Moving to a superior document model meant re-embedding our existing corpus. We selected 30 billion high-priority documents for re-embedding. A migration like this temporarily doubles the embedding load, which made it exactly the right moment to re-evaluate our hardware choices. Figure 2: The doubled inference load from the backfill The preceding figure shows two parallel pipelines sharing the crawl and parse stages, one embedding with the live model into the live index and one re-embedding priority documents with the new model into the new index, which is what doubles the load. This doubling was a clear trigger to reconsider our hardware and optimization choices. Optimization journey AWS Inferentia2 figures refer to performance on the smallest instance type, an Inferentia2 xlarge instance ( inf2.xlarge ), with one chip and two NeuronCores . Our workload runs on a single NeuronCore, so we run Kubernetes pods that pack onto larger instances without leaving any cores idle, giving us container homogeneity across the embedding fleet. The same process runs on a Trainium2 NeuronCore and scales the same way through data parallelism. Our initial Inferentia2 implementation was a straightforward data-parallel, FP16 representation of the model. From that baseline, it became a march to push throughput (docs/sec) as high as possible, using the Neuron SDK and support from the AWS Trainium team. The following chart shows the throughput gains at each milestone. Figure 3: Throughput improvement across optimization milestones Starting from the naive compile, a progressive series of optimizations ultimately delivered roughly a 1.5× throughput improvement. The first was weight layout optimization, which eliminates unnecessary transposes by aligning the weight layout with the scheduling and layout of the broader model. We also enabled autocast, letting the compiler downcast matrix multiplications to lower precision while preserving dynamic range. The downcast outputs met our correctness gate of 0.999 cosine similarity against the reference (see Agentic methodology ), so the accuracy impact was within our acceptance threshold. articles.title: Ted Cruz-led committee approves Trump FCC nominee 15-0 as Democrats boycott vote
articles.content: A Senate committee chaired by Ted Cruz (R-Texas) voted today to approve a Federal Communications Commission nominee, despite accusations that the nominee gave false testimony about her work as a legal advisor for FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. Democrats attempted to prevent a quorum by not showing up, but Cruz proceeded with a Republican-only vote. All 15 Republicans on the Senate Commerce Committee voted to approve Trump nominee Danielle Thumann, while the committee's 13 Democrats were absent. "We're going to be doing our job today, even if the Democrats refuse to show up to do theirs," Cruz said at today's hearing. Nominees are vetted in committees first, and then seek require majority approval from the Senate. Republicans are hoping to get Thumann confirmed before Democrats take Senate control in January. articles.summaryEn: A Senate committee led by Ted Cruz voted 15-0 to approve Trump’s nominee for the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), despite Democrats boycotting the vote. The Republicans aim to confirm nominee Danielle Thumann before the Democrats take control of the Senate in January.

articles.title: 50M unique listeners tune into Apple Music Radio per month, says Zane Lowe
articles.content: An interview with Zane Lowe reveals his thoughts on the hard work of human curation versus cheap and easy algorithms used by other services, plus details of a rocky start at Apple Music . Apple Music at 11 is a big success, but it didn't happen overnight Apple Music Radio started eleven years ago as Beats 1 "worldwide" on Apple Music. It's a 24-hour ad-free radio station available to anyone with an Apple Music app, subscriber or not. In an interview with Billboard , Zane Lowe described starting Apple Music and the live radio station among an audience of "crickets" and growing to 50 million unique listeners per month today. He also boasted about Apple's approach to showcasing new and upcoming artists, broad catalogs, and in-depth interviews. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

articles.title: Apple Releases Safari Technology Preview 257 With Bug Fixes and Performance Improvements
articles.content: Apple today released a new update for Safari Technology Preview , the experimental browser that was first introduced in March 2016. Apple designed ‌Safari Technology Preview‌ to allow users to test features that are planned for future release versions of the Safari browser. ‌Safari Technology Preview‌ 257 includes fixes and updates for Animations, CSS, Canvas, Editing, Forms, Images, JavaScript, Media, Networking, Performance, Rendering, SVG, Scrolling, Security. Web API, Web Extensions, Web Inspector, WebAssembly, Web Driver, WebGL, WebGPU, and WebRTC. The current ‌Safari Technology Preview‌ release is compatible with machines running macOS Tahoe and macOS Golden Gate , the newest version of macOS. The ‌Safari Technology Preview‌ update is available through the Software Update mechanism in System Preferences or System Settings to anyone who has downloaded the browser from Apple's website. Complete release notes for the update are available on the Safari Technology Preview website . Apple's aim with ‌Safari Technology Preview‌ is to gather feedback from developers and users on its browser development process. ‌Safari Technology Preview‌ can run side-by-side with the existing Safari browser and while it is designed for developers, it does not require a developer account to download and use. articles.title: Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits
articles.content: A Ukrainian barrage of missiles and drones collapsed a crucial segment of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s prized Kerch Strait Bridge—and Ukraine’s military pulled off the strike deep within Russian-occupied territory without relying on the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications to guide the missiles in. On the nights of November 15 and November 16, coordinated waves of Ukrainian drones and missiles caused enough damage to collapse one of two steel arches supporting the Kerch bridge’s roadway for automobile traffic, according to an Institute for the Study of War update . Russian sources claimed several hundred Ukrainian drones first overwhelmed Russian air defenses to pave the way for remote-controlled missile strikes focused on the bridge, with the latter prominently including Ukraine’s homegrown Flamingo cruise missile. The Ukrainian operation adapted a Russian battlefield innovation by using drones equipped with mesh radios to create an airborne communications network, according to the Financial Times . Each networked drone acts as a relay node to extend the communication link between human operators and remotely piloted missiles and strike drones. Russia began using the technique to support long-range drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities. Read full article Comments
articles.author: Jeremy Hsu

articles.title: Introducing workload recovery and expanded infrastructure checks on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
articles.content: Large training jobs can fail even when every node looks healthy. A GPU with a subtle fault can pass its stress tests and still return wrong values. When a job stalls on an NCCL timeout, it keeps its GPUs, and Slurm still shows it as running. If a device plugin crashes on one node, the job fails with an error that never mentions the plugin. Teams usually find these problems only after the loss diverges or the job fails, and by then the compute is spent. Each of these failures lowers goodput, the share of your cluster’s time that goes to useful training. Today, we’re introducing workload recovery and infrastructure checks on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod that catch these failures sooner and raise the goodput of your training workloads. SageMaker HyperPod already handles nodes that report hardware faults. The health monitoring agent (HMA) watches each node for GPU errors, deep health checks test nodes during provisioning, and automatic node recovery reboots or replaces faulty hardware. These features look at one node’s hardware at a time. They can’t tell whether the GPUs train correctly, whether a job is still making progress, or whether the Kubernetes components a job depends on are working. In this post, we walk through the three new capabilities that catch these failures. For each one, we show how to set it up and what it reports when it finds a problem: MultiNodeTrainingValidation is a new deep health check for HyperPod clusters orchestrated by Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). When HyperPod provisions an instance, or when you run the check on demand, it trains a small model on the instance and then across instances of the same type. The instance fails if the loss becomes NaN or infinite, or training doesn’t finish in time. The HyperPod Kubernetes Resource Monitoring Agent watches the Kubernetes layer of an EKS cluster for problems such as crash-looping device plugins, missing DaemonSets, and tainted nodes. When a job fails, it reports the pods and nodes involved as Kubernetes events and Amazon CloudWatch logs. Hung job detection finds Slurm jobs that have stopped making progress. An agent on each node watches the job’s output and GPU activity, or log patterns that you define. It writes an event to CloudWatch and can cancel the job so that Slurm requeues it. Why node health alone isn’t enough The existing HyperPod resiliency features check a single node at a time. The health monitoring agent (HMA) watches each node for GPU errors such as Xid and NVLink faults, Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) errors, and kernel errors. The InstanceStress deep health check runs DCGM level 4 diagnostics and tests each instance’s GPUs, GPU memory, NVLink, and EFA devices. The InstanceConnectivity check runs NCCL tests across GPU instances, or NCCOM tests on AWS Trainium. Together, these confirm that each node’s hardware works. They don’t show whether the GPUs compute correctly, whether a job is still making progress, or whether the cluster’s Kubernetes components are healthy. Three kinds of failure get past them: Numerical faults – A GPU can pass every hardware test and still compute wrong results. The first sign is often NaN or infinite loss in a production run. Meta attributed 6 of the 419 unexpected interruptions in its 54-day Llama 3 405B pre-training run to silent data corruption ( The Llama 3 Herd of Models ). Hung jobs – An NCCL timeout, a stalled data pipeline, or a deadlock can stop a job without ending it. The job keeps its GPUs and their memory, and Slurm reports it as running until someone checks the loss curve or the log. Cluster-level failures – Some failures happen in Kubernetes, not in a node’s hardware. A device plugin crash-loops, a required DaemonSet never starts on a new node, or ranks on different nodes fall out of step in an NCCL collective. articles.title: US Bankruptcy Judge Approves Spirit Airlines Data Sale to Google
articles.content: A federal bankruptcy judge has approved Google's $10 million purchase of internal business data from defunct Spirit Airlines during a hearing on Tuesday. Reuters reports: US Bankruptcy Judge Sean Lane, ruling from the bench, cleared the deal after Alphabet's Google agreed last week to implement additional privacy protections for the data, following concerns from labor unions and more than 120 US lawmakers. Discount carrier Spirit halted operations in May. As part of its closure and asset liquidation, Google won an auction in August for employee data from emails, spreadsheets and calendars, as well as for marketing, productivity and operations. Google has said it plans to use the data for product development and AI training. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Stop Fixing Vulnerabilities in Production — Fix Them Where They're Born
articles.content: Introduction Most production vulnerabilities are not introduced in production — they are introduced in the Integrated Development Environment (IDE). Yet historically, most security tooling has operated after code is written, after pull requests are merged, or even worse — after deployment. This reactive approach creates costly rework cycles, slows down release velocity, and increases organizational security risk. Modern DevSecOps fundamentally changes this model. Security must exist inside the developer workflow , not outside of it. Over the past decade, the software supply chain threat landscape has evolved dramatically. Organizations today face risk not only from insecure application code, but also from Open-source dependency vulnerabilities, License compliance violations, misconfigured cloud resources, Insecure CI/CD automation pipelines, compromised build artifacts, & Malicious dependency injection attacks. As organizations accelerate toward microservices, cloud-native architectures, and rapid release cycles, traditional security checkpoints are no longer sufficient. Security must become continuous, automated, and developer-centric. There is always a risk when you try to push a bug fix in production overnight, and you overlook security checks in place, which can expose your production system. The most critical data an organization must safeguard is its customers’ information—whether PII or CPNI. Failure to protect this data can expose customers to risk and lead to serious legal, financial, and reputational consequences for the organization. This article describes a pragmatic and scalable approach to secure development using: SonarQube — Real-time SAST and code quality enforcement inside the IDE JFrog Xray — Software supply chain and open-source dependency vulnerability detection GitHub Copilot (and AI coding assistants) — Accelerating secure remediation while maintaining coding standards DevSecOps pipelines — Enforcing security across the entire software delivery lifecycle 1. The Importance of Developer-Friendly Security The majority of vulnerabilities are introduced during coding. Developer-focused security ensures issues are detected at the earliest possible stage — when they are cheapest and fastest to fix. Common vulnerabilities introduced during development include: · SQL Injection · Improper authorization or missing access validation · Hardcoded credentials or secrets · Unsecured crypto algorithms · Outdated or vulnerable libraries When detected early, these issues can be fixed before code review, build, or deployment phases. Modern tools like SonarQube and Xray help developers understand security risks directly within their development workflow, while AI assistants like GitHub Copilot help apply secure coding fixes quickly and consistently. In large enterprise environments — particularly telecom and financial systems — early detection directly helps with lower remediation costs, fewer production incidents, faster release cycles, and higher developer productivity. 2. Protecting Your Code via SonarQube (Source-Based SAST) SonarQube is a real-time code quality and security analysis tool that runs inside your IDE (like VS Code, IntelliJ, Eclipse). It helps developers detect bugs, security vulnerabilities, and code smells as they write code —before it even reaches CI/CD. It can help with: · Real-time SAST scanning · Security hotspots detection · Code quality rule enforcement · Secure coding rule suggestions You can use SonarQube for Java, Python, JavaScript, C#, C++, and many other programming languages. Key Practices – 2.1 Implement SAST with SonarQube features: · Real-time linting to show real-time code issues the developer can fix. · Autofix suggestions while the developer is coding. · SonarQube connects to enterprise SonarQube using “Connected Mode.” In this mode, the developer’s IDE pulls the same quality profile, rules, and project settings used by SonarQube. · Mandatory security rule set (OWASP Top 10 + CWE) When…

articles.title: Get ready for another critical PHP security release to drop
articles.content: Apologies in advance to all patch managers and security teams that thought they might get a break this week. The PHP Foundation will release a “critical” security update on Thursday between 14:00 and 14:30 UTC. While we don’t have many details about the latest vulnerabilities – these haven’t been leaked like last month’s critical PHP2Shell flaws – a Wednesday advisory said the highest-severity bugs in the upcoming release are rated critical. “The issues rated critical require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups,” the foundation said , urging PHP users to “prepare to upgrade promptly once the releases become available.” We do know that one of the vulnerabilities is another remote code execution (RCE) flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-115560. In October, the PHP Foundation told The Register that it had reserved this CVE identifier for another RCE bug, but added it would not get an emergency fix like the earlier two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities because the third one doesn't pose the same risk. CVE-2026-115560 “requires a very unlikely combination of configuration and specific PHP application code, which we do not expect to occur in practical use of PHP,” Elizabeth Barron, executive director of the PHP Foundation, told The Register at the time. “The issue can be mitigated with a configuration setting. So for the moment the PHP Security Team has only published an informational advisory on the PHP website, explaining exactly this situation.” The earlier informational advisory urged users to “set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector.” These unlikely RCE attacks require an application to set “ session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start() .” Additionally, the session upload progress feature must be enabled, which the PHP Foundation said is very unlikely in real-world applications. The November security release follows a hectic October emergency PHP patch-a-thon , with security teams racing to apply fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively called PHP2Shell, before attackers could abuse the memory-safety flaws in the open source programming language running on about 70 percent of websites. While it took miscreants longer to reverse engineer the PHP2Shell fixes than some researchers had anticipated – and the entire internet didn’t burn down in the meantime – the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) did add the two PHP vulns to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26. Suspected Chinese attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation exploit to root 25 servers, including Palo Alto Networks firewalls linked to US government-affiliated organizations, as early as October 23, according to Dream researchers. The Israeli AI cybersecurity startup said the attackers targeted organizations across the US, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, and “likely still” have persistent, remote access to compromised organizations’ networks. ®

articles.title: Introducing the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard
articles.content: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart gives you hundreds of open-weight foundation models you can deploy quickly. That choice is powerful, but it also creates a real question: Which model should you start with? Comparing models usually means reading model cards one at a time and hunting for benchmark scores that different sources published under different conditions. Then you still must guess how each model will perform, and what it will cost, for your use case. Today we are launching the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard , a new way to compare JumpStart models side by side on quality, speed, and cost, directly in Amazon SageMaker Studio. In this post, we explain what the leaderboard shows, define the key terms in plain language, and walk through how to go from a shortlist to a deployed model. What is the JumpStart Model Leaderboard? The leaderboard is a new view of the JumpStart base models page in SageMaker Studio, right next to the Categories and All models views. It uses the same search bar and filters you already know, and it opens on a leaderboard of large language models (LLMs). You see rankings immediately without answering setup questions first. For each model, it shows two kinds of information: Quality scores on three public benchmarks (BIG-Bench Hard, GPQA Diamond, and MMLU-Pro) that AWS runs itself, using the same evaluation setup for every model so the numbers are comparable. Performance and cost metrics that AWS measures by sending a standardized test workload to an endpoint using each JumpStart deployment configuration, so you see how fast a model responds and what it costs to run. Because both kinds of numbers come from the same place and the same method, you can make a like-for-like comparison instead of stitching together data from different websites. At launch, the leaderboard covers 70+ models from providers including Meta, Google, Qwen, IBM, and Arcee, with more added over time. The following screenshot shows the leaderboard in SageMaker Studio, with benchmark scores, performance metrics, and estimated cost for each model. Figure 1: Leaderboard overview in SageMaker Studio Key concepts This section defines the terms the leaderboard uses: the quality benchmarks, the use case profiles and optimization goals that shape the performance numbers, and the performance metrics themselves. Quality benchmarks A benchmark is a standardized test: a fixed set of questions with known answers. Running every model through the same test gives you a score you can compare. At launch, the leaderboard reports three reasoning benchmarks for LLMs: Benchmark What it measures, in plain terms BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) A set of challenging tasks that require multi-step reasoning, such as logical deduction, tracking objects, and multi-step arithmetic. GPQA Diamond Graduate-level science questions that are difficult to answer by searching the web. A good signal of deep reasoning. MMLU-Pro Broad knowledge and reasoning across many subjects, such as science, law, and engineering, using harder multiple-choice questions. Higher is better for all three. The leaderboard shows each benchmark separately rather than blending them into one number. That keeps the results transparent: You can weigh the benchmarks that matter for your application and check each score against the public definition of the benchmark. Use case profiles and optimization goals Speed and cost depend on your workload and on how the model is deployed. Two menus above the leaderboard control which performance and cost numbers you see: Use case profile. Select the profile closest to your workload from the View benchmarks for your use case menu. The default is Max Context. The profile changes only the performance and cost metrics. Quality benchmark scores are the same for every profile. Optimization goal. For each profile, a model can have several deployment configurations, and the leaderboard shows metrics for one at a time. Choose which one with the Optimized for menu. The…

articles.title: Trump abandons his FDA nominee, and Senate scraps vote on his NSF pick
articles.content: In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump's pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation. Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy's decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats. In her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated. The questions she dodged included those on how she would handle the FDA's current safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone, which extensive data has established is extremely safe. She also wouldn't say whether she agreed with Trump when he falsely claimed the measles vaccine is "quite lethal" or that children are given vaccine doses the "size of a soda bottle." Overton repeatedly refused to answer whether Trump could ever be wrong. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Google acquires Seattle startup Howie and its AI scheduling assistant
articles.content: Howie co-founders Dave Newman, left and Austin Petersmith. (Howie Photo) Google is bringing Seattle-based Howie , maker of an AI scheduling assistant that works from your inbox, into its Google Labs division. Terms of the deal were not disclosed this week. Google Labs, the company’s experimental arm, announced the acquisition in a post on X , saying it “can’t wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses.” Howie CEO and co-founder Austin Petersmith said on LinkedIn that the team will continue building Howie at Google. “Howie has always been built on top of Gmail and Google Calendar, so Google Labs is the perfect place for us to take this product to the next level,” he wrote. Petersmith co-founded Howie around 2023 with CTO Dave Newman . The two first worked together in 2013 at Assembly, which Newman co-founded, and prototyped an AI assistant in 2015 before deciding the market wasn’t ready. We’re excited to welcome Howie to Google Labs! The @Howie_ai team has spent years figuring out scheduling and calendar management. We can’t wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses 🤝 https://t.co/8bzjebeGdD — Google Labs (@GoogleLabs) November 16, 2026 Users cc Howie on an email thread, and it coordinates meeting times, adds events to calendars, follows up as needed and flags scheduling conflicts. Customers set their own rules in an open-ended preferences document, such as “if it’s a pitch call, set it to 25 minutes and use Zoom.” Behind the scenes, Howie ran tasks through fine-tuned language models and looped in human scheduling experts when the AI wasn’t confident. Howie raised a $6 million seed round led by True Ventures in September 2025, when it launched publicly out of private beta. At the time, it had more than 1,000 paying customers, including startup founders, venture capitalists, recruiters, consultants and journalists, and was scheduling more than 5,000 meetings a week. The deal comes as Google and rivals including OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta race to build AI agents that complete tasks on behalf of users. Google Labs acquired music generation platform ProducerAI earlier this year .

articles.title: An updated Clairic and Clairic-flash are now open-weight, from the new Workers AI Superintelligence team
articles.content: Cloudflare has become a neolab. We’re building our own frontier AI models for our customers and the open-source community. Today, we’re announcing two open-weight model releases: We’re introducing an updated version of Clairic . Since the preview, we’ve improved extraction from complex documents including images and PDFs (new!), with more reliable handling of tables, lists, and dates, and better grounding of answers in the source material. We’re introducing Clairic-flash , a lighter, faster version of Clairic that delivers strong extraction and prediction performance in a compact, 9-billion-parameter model. Both extraction models are hosted on Workers AI and full open weights are available on Hugging Face . We’re also excited to re-introduce ourselves as the Workers AI superintelligence team, the frontier AI research team behind Clef , Clairic, and lots more in the works. This team is working quickly to push the AI frontier and build useful models for Cloudflare’s customers and the open source community. A new version of Clairic: redesigned after the preview release Since announcing Clairic in preview, we have received a ton of use cases and helpful feedback on how customers wanted to use an extraction model. We heard about use cases ranging from extracting data from images like receipts to reading values from support tickets. We knew that we wanted extraction to be the clear focus for the model, so it had to excel at reading from unstructured data. We decided to go back to the drawing board with Clairic and redesigned our architecture, differentiating this new version of Clairic from our preview release. For ordinary text and number extraction fields, we now use parallel slot autoregressive generation instead of a single forward pass. Each field uses the tokens it has already written to choose its next token, then stops at its own end marker. All the fields advance together in the serving batch, still giving lightning-fast latency per request. This boosted our accuracy in extraction for both text and images, and the trade-off in accuracy offsets the small latency cost. For computation, estimation, and extraction use cases, we trained special heads that can handle estimates, forecasts, durations, calculated dates, and explicit arithmetic. Although the model architecture evolved, we kept the parts of the typed API interface that make the answers useful: confidence scores, character spans, and probabilities are still intact with every request. The model is still incredibly fast and cheap. From the evals below, you can see how our newer versions of Clairic have greatly improved on extraction across text, images, PDFs, and more. articles.title: Best Buy Resumes Blu-ray Sales
articles.content: Best Buy has resumed selling Blu-ray movies directly through its website and physical stores after exiting the physical media business in 2023. The retailer currently offers a limited selection of 15 Blu-ray listings, including new releases like The Odyssey and Project Hail Mary and older titles like It's a Wonderful Life (1943), Saving Private Ryan (1998), and The Godfather (1972). Ars Technica reports: Overall, the sales of Blu-rays and DVDs in the US have been steadily declining, and annual consumer spending dropped 9.3 percent from 2024 to 2025, according to the Digital Entertainment Group (DEG). During this same time, however, consumer spending on 4K Blu-ray discs specifically increased 12 percent year over year, per DEG. "We're seeing a lot of evidence, including at the Criterion Mobile Closet, that more young people are thinking about physical media in a different way," Peter Becker, president of Criterion, which sells Blu-rays and DVDs online, told the Los Angeles Times in February. "In an age where so much is available to us on demand, it becomes increasingly important to us." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: How Airbnb uses cost per task to operate coding agents on Amazon Bedrock
articles.content: Amazon Bedrock provides access to foundation models from multiple providers through a common API, with AWS managing the model infrastructure. It integrates with AWS access controls and monitoring, and processes prompts, code, and model responses within AWS. As coding agents move into production, changes in models and usage can affect latency, capacity, and cost. Amazon Bedrock runtime metrics in Amazon CloudWatch help teams investigate latency increases, throttling, and changes in token consumption. Evaluations, or evals, complement these operational metrics by assessing the quality of an agent’s work on a fixed set of representative tasks. In this post, we show how Airbnb evaluates models for coding agents and monitors their use on Amazon Bedrock. We explain how cost per task guides model selection and how production data helps us revisit those choices as usage changes. We also describe the runtime signals used to investigate latency, throttling, and spend. At Airbnb, thousands of engineers and engineering-adjacent people use AirChat, our internal tool for running coding agents, every week. The agents send their model requests through our large language model (LLM) gateway, which runs on Amazon Bedrock. Bedrock processes Airbnb’s code, prompts, and model responses within AWS. Eight new models came out in about five weeks. By mid-October, about two thirds of the requests our engineers sent through coding agents went to those new models. Each release can change output tokens, cost, latency and capacity at once, and the benchmark charts published with a launch don’t show how a model handles our engineers’ work. So we run two systems side by side. Before a rollout, we run evals on our own tasks to measure each model’s score and cost per task. Cost per task is the list-price cost of all the tokens an agent uses to finish one task. After a rollout, observability shows us what changed in production. When production usage doesn’t match the eval results, we find out why. Solution overview You can diagnose most production problems with a few signals in the AWS/Bedrock namespace in CloudWatch: Latency: InvocationLatency , TimeToFirstToken , OutputTokenCount , and output tokens per second (OTPS), which you derive. Throttling: InvocationThrottles , plus the tokens each request reserves against your quota, which you publish yourself. Bedrock also publishes EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage , which measures your estimated tokens per minute (TPM) quota consumption, including cache write tokens and output burndown multipliers, across all inference APIs ( Converse , InvokeModel , ConverseStream , and InvokeModelWithResponseStream ). You can use this metric to set proactive alarms before reaching your quota limit, track your quota consumption across your models, and request further quota increases before usage is rate limited. Cost: InputTokenCount (uncached input), CacheReadInputTokenCount , CacheWriteInputTokenCount and OutputTokenCount , each priced at its own rate. Cache reads cost less than uncached input, and cache writes can cost more depending on the model. A lower cache hit rate can increase cost per request. On top of these metrics, we add cost per task. Our evals measure a score and a cost per task for every model and every reasoning effort we allow. Reasoning effort is a setting that controls how much a model reasons before it responds. We use the results to choose each default, which is the model and effort that our coding tools use unless an engineer picks another, and each effort ceiling, which is the highest effort we allow for a model. Architecture Engineers run AirChat on their AirDev workspaces, which are personal development machines in the cloud. They can also hand a task to AirChat Remote, which runs cloud agents in separate cloud workspaces while the engineer does something else. Both paths go through our LLM gateway to Amazon Bedrock. articles.title: Anthropic decides to go head-to-head with GTA VI release, schedules IPO for the same day
articles.content: Well, it’s official: Anthropic will become the first publicly-traded frontier AI lab in history come the opening of markets on Thursday. The company kicked off its IPO roadshow last week, announcing plans to offer 825 million shares with an IPO price between $70 and $78 a share when sales begin Thursday. The company's most recent SEC filing cites that price range but allows for the possibility of a higher price, which should be determined Wednesday night. Late on Wednesday, Bloomberg reported that Anthropic would price at $83, citing people familiar. Whatever the case, Anthropic is likely to be valued at more than $1 trillion. Anthropic’s debutante ball has been on the horizon for a while, and documents leaked in late September made it all the more inevitable as the company’s finances revved up and it sought to capture the momentum of its best quarter to date before things start to tail off. The company revised its IPO documents on November 2, warning that the 12x growth it was touting was unlikely to continue in the long term due to compute infrastructure investments to the tune of nearly $900 billion it was on the hook for over the next few years. "In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, our revenue was $33.2 billion, representing a year-over-year growth rate of 1,206%," the revised prospectus reads. "We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates, and we cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all." It’s possible, in other words, that Anthropic may never be a money maker despite the hype and its position as the first mover. The IPO prospectus is short on answers to critical questions and leaves a lot unanswered - like, for example, whether it’s going to actually be able to pay its bills. "Our ability to meet the substantial and growing financial obligations of these requirements to secure compute depends on our ability to generate significant revenue growth," the updated prospectus admits. Investors don’t seem to care right now, though. Anthropic already has compute commitments amounting to roughly $70.7 billion in the next 12 months. That’s just shy of its $81 billion run-rate as of October 31. Expect more hot air to be injected tomorrow, adding additional surface tension and the possibility of even more losses if, and when, this monster pops. ®

articles.title: Design responsible AI controls for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
articles.content: A customer support chatbot that queries historical tickets and knowledge base articles stored in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition can deliver fast, context-aware answers. However, it also introduces challenges around privacy, accuracy, safety, and governance, especially when the underlying data contains sensitive customer information. In this post, we map the eight AWS Responsible AI (RAI) dimensions to Aurora PostgreSQL capabilities. We then walk through a design pattern for the Explainability dimension, using a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) based customer support chatbot as the reference use case. This post implements one dimension, Explainability, in depth. Treat it as Part 1 of a series rather than a full build-out of all eight. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition makes it more straightforward to operationalize responsible AI through its native Aurora Machine Learning (Aurora ML) capabilities. With Aurora ML, you can invoke Amazon SageMaker endpoints and Amazon Bedrock foundation models directly from SQL, without data movement, custom extract, transform, and load (ETL) pipelines, or complex integrations. This post uses Aurora ML to generate vector embeddings from SQL, keeping the embedding pipeline inside the database layer. AWS defines eight core Responsible AI dimensions, published through the AWS Well-Architected Responsible AI Lens , Amazon Bedrock Guardrails , and the Responsible Use of AI Guide . These dimensions (Fairness, Explainability, Privacy and Security, Safety, Controllability, Veracity and Robustness, Governance, and Transparency) provide a structured framework for evaluating and implementing trustworthy AI systems. Use case overview Customer support systems often struggle to provide accurate, context-aware responses while maintaining privacy and compliance. Consider a customer support chatbot built on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL that uses RAG with pgvector embeddings, Amazon Bedrock model inference, and AWS Responsible AI guardrails to deliver grounded, explainable responses. A customer can ask questions such as “Why was my last bill high?” or “Where is my last order?” and receive accurate answers with citations, while sensitive data remains obscured through personally identifiable information (PII) redaction and access controls. Mapping the AWS Responsible AI dimensions to Aurora PostgreSQL The following table maps the eight AWS Responsible AI dimensions to practical implementation strategies for a customer support chatbot built on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition. It highlights how database features, AWS AI services, and governance controls work together to deliver a trustworthy, secure, and explainable RAG-based chatbot. Fairness Chatbot should provide equal quality responses regardless of language, region, or customer profile Bias testing using diverse support queries. Decouple demographics from embeddings. Metadata filtering and multilingual testing. pgvector, JSONB metadata, SQL filtering, views Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation, Amazon SageMaker Clarify 2. Explainability Users and support teams should know why the chatbot gave a specific answer Log retrieved chunks, similarity scores, and citations. RAG tracing with source attribution. Full interaction logging. chat_interactions table, array columns, JSONB logs, pgvector similarity Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel 3. Privacy and Security Protect customer PII such as name, phone, and order details in tickets PII redaction before embedding. Row-Level Security (RLS), encryption, IAM auth, RBAC, and anonymization. Row-Level Security, pgcrypto, roles, policies Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, AWS KMS, Amazon Comprehend, AWS IAM 4. articles.title: ‘Sister isn’t free’: Melinda French Gates fact-checks viral ‘SNL’ sketch on eldercare
articles.content: “Saturday Night Live” host John Mulaney during a fake ad about senior care called “Sister.” (YouTube screen grab / SNL) A “Saturday Night Live” skit about caring for aging relatives touched a viral nerve after it aired over the weekend, including with Melinda French Gates, who offered her own “fact check” on the too-close-to-home comedy. The sketch, a fake commercial, stars host John Mulaney as a man who has found an easy way to care for his aging father without upending his own life: “Sister,” an “elder care system” that is free and is, in fact, his sister. French Gates wrote on Instagram this week that the sketch “is funny because it’s a little too true.” Using research from Pivotal, her investment and philanthropic organization, she went through the ad’s claims one by one and found that most held up: Sister will provide. True, French Gates said, citing AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving. Among adults ages 55 to 64, women are nearly 40% more likely than men to care for an older relative, and nearly 40% more likely to provide constant care. She’ll quit her job. “Mostly true,” at least the job part. Catalyst found that 42% of women who voluntarily left jobs in 2025 cited caregiving as the main reason. Paid help is pricey. “True, unfortunately.” New America puts the average home health aide at more than $6,600 a month, and 24-hour care can top $25,000. Sister may break down. Also true. In the Caregiving in the U.S. 2025 report, nearly two-thirds of caregivers said they were under moderate or high emotional stress, and women felt the strain more than men did. “Free” is misleading. French Gates said Sister isn’t free; she’s the one paying for the care, in lost wages, stalled careers, thinner retirement savings and less time for her own life. French Gates has made women’s health and caregiving central to her work since she stepped down as co-chair of the Gates Foundation in 2024. She left with $12.5 billion to put toward her work on behalf of women and families. Much of that work runs through Pivotal, the Seattle-area organization she founded to handle her philanthropy and investments. In June she pledged another $215 million for women’s health, which brought her giving in that area to more than $600 million over two years. The pledge included $10 million to the Menopause Society for better menopause care in the U.S. The sketch has been shared widely across the country this week, in part because it lines up so closely with the research. In its own analysis, The New York Times cited studies showing that daughters generally provide at least twice as much care to aging parents as sons do. The U.S., unlike many wealthy countries, offers no federal paid leave or long-term care insurance for family caregivers. French Gates said she welcomed the conversation. “I’m so glad we’re talking about this, and laughing about it,” she wrote on Instagram. “We need more honesty about what caring for loved ones really takes and why so much of that work falls to women. But I’d love for the day to come when these jokes don’t pack quite the same punch — because we’ve made it so much easier to care for the people we love.”

articles.title: Absolute Batman can save DC Studios
articles.content: With James Gunn and Peter Safran out as the co-heads of DC Studios following Skydance's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery , it's unclear what will become of the cinematic universe that was building around movies like last year's Superman . Though Gunn's Man of Tomorrow feature might still come out , it seems like his larger vision for the DC Universe may be tossed out by DC Studios' newly appointed CEO, Jeremy Latcham . Gunn was taking his time fleshing out the DCU with relatively less high-profile characters like Peacemaker , Supergirl , and Clayface . But Latcham has reportedly received a mandate from Skydance CEO David Ellison to fast-track … Read the full story at The Verge.

articles.title: Apple Card Offers New Users Double Daily Cash for a Year
articles.content: Apple is aiming to get people to sign up for the Apple Card over the holidays by offering a 2X Daily Cash bonus for new users. iPhone users who sign up for an Apple Card by December 10 can earn up to six percent Daily Cash on purchases for the first year after opening the account, with Apple offering up to $1,000 total bonus Daily Cash. The promo doubles the standard Daily Cash back rewards: 6% - At Apple and participating merchants when using ‌Apple Card‌ with Apple Pay . 4% - On purchases made using an ‌Apple Card‌ with ‌Apple Pay‌. 2% - On purchases made with the physical ‌Apple Card‌ or virtual card number (no ‌Apple Pay‌). After a year or when the $1,000 bonus Daily Cash limit is reached, Daily Cash will revert to the standard one, two, and three percent rewards. Getting the full bonus amount would require spending about $33,333 at six percent, $50,000 at four percent, or $100,000 at two percent, so for many users, the bonus cash earned will be less than Apple's maximum. Those interested in the deal will need to apply through the promo website , as Apple says the deal may not be available elsewhere. The promotion is not available to current ‌Apple Card‌ holders or those who have had an ‌Apple Card‌ in the past. ‌Apple Card‌ continues to be available only in the U.S. Tag: Apple Card This article, " Apple Card Offers New Users Double Daily Cash for a Year " first appeared on MacRumors.com Discuss this article in our forums

articles.title: AI found more critical bugs in another widely used technology running 225M websites
articles.content: Hot on the heels of serious vulnerabilities in seemingly every other widely used software powering the entire internet, F5 today released emergency patches for 10 bugs in open source NGINX. These include critical remote code execution flaws that let attackers hijack NGINX servers with HTTP/2 enabled, as well as the millions of websites running NGINX, to steal sensitive data and disrupt services. “At this time, we have found no evidence of active exploitation of any of these vulnerabilities in the wild,” and F5 spokesperson told The Register . “We continue to monitor closely and will share updates via myF5 as we learn more.” As with all of the other recently disclosed vulnerabilities in foundational technologies like PHP, Apache, and Java, these critical NGINX bugs were uncovered by researchers using AI. One of them has been hiding in the code for at least 10 years. Tomer Schwartz, Wiz’s chief technology officer of exposure management and AppSec, helped find the bug, along with researchers from Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint working independently. Schwartz told The Register that this wave of AI-discovered flaws “point to a new reality.” “We need to treat every internet-connected system as potentially vulnerable,” Schwartz said. “AI has changed not only which vulnerabilities can be found, but how quickly longstanding risks can become real threats.” NGINX is the world’s most widely used open source web server, handling HTTPS requests and routing incoming traffic to the right application or API. It powers about a third of all websites (around 225 million ), and F5 maintains the open source version. On Wednesday, F5 published an out-of-band security notification that addressed 10 CVEs in open source NGINIX. If you run NGINX, update to 1.31.9 as soon as possible. CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 Two of the vulns are especially serious as they allow a remote attacker to execute code on the NGINX server without authentication. These two, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 , both received a critical, 9.2 CVSS rating, and CVE-2026-123007 affects versions dating back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server. All of the security shops listed earlier independently found at least one of these two CVEs - most, if not all, with an AI assist - and reported them to F5. “Both vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues in how NGINX handles HTTP/2 traffic,” Schwartz and fellow Wiz kid Nir Ohfeld said in a Wednesday blog about the two bugs. “In CVE-2026-123633, a connection's memory is freed while a request still needs it, creating a use-after-free. In CVE-2026-123007, incorrect flow-control accounting leads to an invalid memory copy.” Rapid7’s team also published a proof-of-concep t to demonstrate leveraging CVE-2026-123007 for unauthenticated remote code execution against a vulnerable linux/amd64 Docker image running nginx version 1.31.8. Xint found three other NGINX flaws, plus a separate vulnerability in the Linux kernel that can be chained with any of the five NGINX vulnerabilities to gain root privileges on the host. The research team dubbed the six bugs “ nginx2root .” The AI-powered offensive security firm also published videos demonstrating attacks using CVE-2026-123007 to execute commands as the NGINX worker inside a container, and then using the kernel vulnerability to escalate to root on the host. These attacks work on AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, and bare-metal servers. AI-powered bug hunting for the win? "While preparing for ZeroDay Cloud 2026, a Xint researcher found CVE-2026-123007," the company said in a Wednesday blog. "A few days later, a fully automated Xint scan found the other four without human guidance." All of these newly-disclosed CVEs point to a larger security issue - especially in light of Tuesday’s Java4Shell , found by AI-bug-hunting-outfit Calif, PHP2Shell (Calif was one of the firms that also used AI to find and…

articles.title: AMD’s Twitter brag that it ‘loves gamers’ met with savage Community Note
articles.content: AMD Japan's X account has been met with sharp reproach after claiming the company loves gamers and values its interactions with gamers above all else, with commenters and even a community note expressing dissent at the sentiment, owing to AMD's comments on its "data center-first" ethos and a commitment to AI that has driven the price of consumer PC gaming up to nearly unaffordable levels. Quoting a Tom's Hardware post on the X social network discussing CEO Dr. Lisa Su meeting gamers and autographing a GPU , the AMD Japan account was quick to seize the moment. "AMD values its interactions with gamers above all else," the post read, but it was met with a stark reminder that gamers don't feel the same way. The post soon received a new community note that pointed out that AMD's own CEO doesn't agree. In fact, Su was quoted as saying that AMD is now "a data center-first company," with the note also pointing to the fact that AMD's data center revenue increased 97% year-over-year, as per its Q3 2026 earnings report. That equates to around $8.5 billion in revenue, while client and gaming revenue fell 8% to $3.7 billion. Gaming alone was down 40%. At the time, Su said that AMD expected its server revenue to double year over year in 2027, with its data center AI revenue growing at an even faster rate. "As a result, we expect data center to be more than eighty percent of our total revenue in 2027 and to drive the majority of our revenue and earnings growth," the CEO said during the company's earnings call. ゲーマーとの交流を何よりも大切にするAMD。コミュニティと直接つながり、その声に耳を傾け続ける姿勢こそAMDの強みです。AMD loves gamers. 🎮 November 17, 2026 By comparison, the same call heard Su say that, in 2027, AMD was "planning for PC market unit shipments to decline by a double-digit percentage." With this all in mind, it's perhaps no surprise that the AMD Japan X account stirred such a strong response from gamers who feel that AMD has left them behind in search of a more lucrative data center market. AMD is certainly not alone in that regard. Nvidia, once the darling of the PC component enthusiast, is now focused on AI data center components instead. The company's high-performance AI chips are so capable that they're export-controlled, something that, among other reasons, will put former CEO Jensen Huang in front of a House Foreign Affairs panel in December. As for AMD, its ill-timed, misjudged X post ended with "AMD loves gamers." Gamers would appear to disagree.

articles.title: Nvidia GeForce driver bug reportedly hammers SSDs with up to 30GB of writes per hour
articles.content: Nvidia’s GeForce driver 621.14 is reportedly causing excessive background writes on idle PCs, inducing extra wear on SSDs. One user measured about 3GB an hour on the susceptible driver, and another mentioned estimated up to 30GB/hour on the newer 621.24. This follows a similar-looking bug from AMD’s video driver discovered last month. The bug is described by user Andergraude in an Nvidia forum post as “new in 621.14,” which came out on Nov. 4, who says it operates by “continuously [rewriting] the binary log file” with “real writes” to the drive. The writes are coming from the NVDisplay.Container.exe process, or the “NVIDIA Display Container LS” service, which logs to the nvlog.nvlgstg file. This background service is necessary for running the Nvidia Control Panel and App. It’s not clear what’s written in the log, and not every system is necessarily impacted. The “real writes” point comes from the fact that a per-process write counter is not the same as writes reaching the drive. The measurements came from Windows Resource Monitor, Windows performance counters, and CrystalDiskInfo. The Data Units Written counter matched Windows’ reporting. This test showed 515MB of process I/O coming with 270MB of total writes to the C: drive over five minutes. That works out to roughly 3GB per hour, in line with the user’s own estimate. Worse, “the write volume increases as the file grows.” Stopping the service and deleting the log can temporarily reduce the writes. With the previous driver version 621.01, the writes totaled less than 2MB per five minutes, and a second user in the thread confirmed that a rollback helps. Mitigation attempts, such as three clean reinstalls with the help of DDU from that second user, did not fix the problem. The writing process also impacted gaming and video performance, potentially causing hitching, which suggests it gets worse under load. Another user, AyzekUorren, in a separate thread about driver 621.24, which came out Nov. 12, says that it could get up to “about 30gb per 1h” or even “70gb or even more” with longer sessions. This is even with telemetry disabled in the Nvidia App. Noted is that every Alt+Tab added 500MB to 1GB of writes, at least for this user. In AMD’s case, it was the External Events Utility, or atieclxx.exe, that exhibited constant writes on an idle PC. In that case, the AMD utility was reportedly copying its own executable every second. To put the impact into context, the AMD bug had rates reported between 0.3 and 5MB/s while total drive writes in the 621.14 test measured around 0.9MB/s. The Nvidia numbers are somewhat alarming, given that a typical 1TB SSD is rated for 600TB of writes over a standard five-year warranty. Even at 270MB per five minutes, this could be about 28TB per year — for a never-sleeping PC — which is reaching toward 5% of the drive’s rated endurance, although the writes include everything the system is writing and realistic uptime will be less. However, at the higher end — 30GB per hour, at eight hours a day — one could see 15% of drive endurance worn every year for nothing. This doesn’t make it a drive killer, but given how much users value drive endurance , especially with SSD prices as they are, avoiding unnecessary writes like this is certainly a priority. To see if you’re affected, check Resource Monitor and look for the telltale NVDisplay.Container.exe and the nvlog.nvlgstg file in the list. You can also check the SMART Data Units Written value with CrystalDiskInfo or equivalent, such as your drive’s SSD toolbox. At this time, no fix or hotfix has been announced, and the best workaround is to do a rollback. A similar issue in the past, fixed with driver update 471.96 back in 2021, was covered by Nvidia’s release notes. As it stands, Nvidia has “N/A” for 621.24’s Open Issues, and the company has not acknowledged the bug. For the AMD bug, the driver wasn't fixed for over three weeks (and came as an optional update).

articles.title: Bank CEOs, NSA Tell Congress That AI-Driven Patches Are Behind Outages
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from The Washington Sun: Wall Street executives and the National Security Agency have told members of Congress that this week's widespread tech outages were caused by attempts to fix vulnerabilities identified by artificial intelligence, according to three sources familiar with the private conversations. [...] "These models are identifying massive vulnerabilities, and that increases the urgency to patch right away," said one congressional official briefed on the matter. "They're trying to push through a lot of patches all at once -- more than the system was designed for." On Monday, banks such as JP Morgan Chase blamed software-related bugs for the service issues. On Tuesday, the NSA said that "scheduled routine maintenance" was responsible for the "temporary degradation" of some of its networks. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told CNBC on Tuesday that "they're pushing new technology on top of really old computer systems, and it just seems to overwhelm the system. ... We're going to see more of this as new technology rolls out." "There's some sense in which this is reassuring, in that it means there's not an attack. But it shows the extent to which safety critical infrastructure we rely on is based on software with large vulnerabilities on legacy systems," said Nathan Calvin, the chief strategy officer at Encode. "Updating those is going to be a rocky process, and as we get more advanced models this won't be a one and done thing -- we'll continue to find more vulnerabilities." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.content: U.S. lawmakers are warning Apple and other tech companies to crack down on apps that generate nonconsensual nude images or face congressional action. US senators press Apple over App Store nudify apps Three U.S. senators pressed Apple and Google on Wednesday over apps that generate nonconsensual nude images. The senators also challenged Meta over paid ads for the apps on Facebook and Instagram. In October, the Tech Transparency Project found 135 apps across both the App Store and Google Play available to accounts set up for 13-year-olds. Apple and Google removed the apps flagged by researchers, but those apps still worked on phones where they were already installed. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

articles.title: Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
articles.content: Many teams that build applications self-host their identity provider (IdP), such as Keycloak or PingFederate, inside a private network. These IdPs usually present a TLS server certificate from a private certificate authority (CA). With private CA support in AgentCore Identity , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, your agents can now connect to these IdPs while trusting the private CA that your organization already uses. AgentCore Identity now supports private CA certificates for private identity providers. You store the PEM-encoded CA certificate in AWS Secrets Manager or Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) and reference it from your credential provider . The CA certificate contains only the public certificate, not its private key. AgentCore Identity uses it to validate the server certificate presented by your IdP’s discovery, JSON Web Key Set (JWKS), and token endpoints. The CA certificate must be a root or intermediate CA certificate. In this post, we show you how to issue an IdP certificate with AWS Private Certificate Authority. We then configure an AgentCore Identity credential provider to trust it and rotate the CA while minimizing downtime. We also show how to protect the CA certificate so that only your IdP team can change it. Although AgentCore Identity supports any private CA, including enterprise, third-party, and self-signed root CAs, the walkthrough in this post uses AWS Private CA and Keycloak as the IdP. Solution overview Consider an agent that needs to call an internal wiki API protected by your Keycloak IdP. The agent runs on AgentCore Runtime , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which hosts your agent code. To get an OAuth 2.0 access token from Keycloak, the agent uses an AgentCore Identity credential provider, which holds the IdP connection details and client credentials. The following diagram shows this setup. Keycloak runs in your virtual private cloud (VPC) behind an internal Application Load Balancer. The load balancer presents an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) private certificate signed by AWS Private CA. The CA certificate that AgentCore Identity trusts is stored in Secrets Manager or Amazon S3. AgentCore Identity reaches the IdP privately through Amazon VPC Lattice , which connects to your VPC through a resource gateway , an entry point for VPC Lattice traffic into your VPC. VPC Lattice is required for private CA support. If you choose the managed option, AgentCore Identity creates and manages the VPC Lattice resources for you. Figure 1: Connecting AgentCore Identity to a self-hosted IdP that uses a private CA The flow works as follows: You store the CA certificate in Secrets Manager or Amazon S3. You create a credential provider that points to your IdP and to the CA certificate. AgentCore Identity reads the CA certificate and checks that it’s a valid CA certificate. Your agent requests an access token from AgentCore Identity. AgentCore Identity connects to the IdP through VPC Lattice and checks the load balancer certificate against your CA. The IdP issues the token and AgentCore Identity returns it to your agent. Agents that use machine-to-machine, on-behalf-of, and user-delegated flows can also use the private CA without changing their code. Prerequisites To follow this walkthrough, you need: An AWS account with access to the AgentCore console , in a supported AWS Region where AgentCore Identity supports private IdPs. A self-hosted, OpenID Connect (OIDC) compliant IdP that runs in your VPC, with an OAuth client registered for your agent. The networking requirements, including subnets, security groups, and a private hosted zone for the IdP hostname, are described in Connect to private identity providers . The latest version of the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and OpenSSL . Permission to create credential providers, plus read access to the CA certificate. AgentCore Identity reads the certificate with the credentials of the principal that calls CreateOauth2CredentialProvider…
